description.en: Turn the inventory into a matrix that grants each role or identity the minimum actions on each data class and data type it needs, using the organisation's classification labels. Identify combinations of duties that must not sit with one role, such as preparing training data and approving the trained model, and split them. Attach the matrix and the conflict record.

evidenceHint.en: Access control matrix by role, data class and permitted action, with the segregation-of-duties conflict record

text.en: Group AI data by classification label and by type: training, inference, model parameters.
Grant each role only the actions its inventory row justifies on each group.
Remove default or broad permissions that no inventory row supports.
List the duty combinations that must be split and assign them to separate roles.
Record who the data owner is for each group and date the matrix.

title.en: Configure role permissions on AI data stores, ML platforms, APIs and applications

description.en: Implement the matrix at every layer where AI data sits or is served: databases, data lakes, document stores and file storage; ML development and MLOps platforms down to project, experiment, dataset and model; APIs exposing data or model functions; and applications that display AI output. Manage roles centrally through the identity platform where it is feasible. Attach permission exports from each layer.

evidenceHint.en: Permission exports from each AI data store, ML platform, API and application, mapped to matrix rows

text.en: Create the matrix roles in the central identity platform where the layer supports it.
Apply role permissions on each data repository holding AI data.
Restrict ML platform projects, experiments, datasets and models by role.
Add role checks to APIs that expose AI data or model functions.
Configure consuming applications to show users only data their role permits.
Export the resulting permissions from each layer for the record.

title.en: Enforce strong authentication for people and machine identities using AI data

description.en: Require multi-factor authentication for every person who reaches AI data, and give each model, pipeline and service account its own managed credential, such as a certificate or service principal, held in a secrets manager and rotated on a schedule the organisation sets. Where a component processes particularly sensitive data, consider requiring it to attest its identity before it may read. Attach the configuration and the credential register.

evidenceHint.en: Multi-factor authentication policy configuration and the register of non-human credentials with storage location and rotation date

text.en: Turn on multi-factor authentication for every human role in the matrix.
Issue each non-human identity its own credential rather than a shared one.
Store every machine credential in the secrets manager and record its location.
Record the rotation schedule chosen and the last rotation date per credential.
Record whether attestation is required for components reading the most sensitive data.

title.en: Review AI data access logs for denied attempts and unusual access

description.en: Make sure every access to AI data, granted or refused, is logged with the identity, the data, the action and the time, and review the logs on the cadence the organisation sets for repeated refusals, access outside normal patterns and other policy breaches. Attach the review record with any follow-up.

evidenceHint.en: Access log review record for the period, listing anomalies and denied-attempt patterns found and the follow-up on each

text.en: Confirm logging captures identity, data accessed, action and timestamp on each layer.
Confirm refused attempts are logged as well as successful ones.
Pull the period's logs and filter for repeated refusals by one identity.
Look for access at unusual times, volumes or to data outside the role's normal set.
Record each anomaly with the person following it up and the outcome.

title.en: Recertify AI data access with data owners and revoke unconfirmed grants

description.en: At the interval the organisation has chosen, send each data owner the current grants on their AI data, have them confirm or reject each, and revoke what they reject. Check also that leavers, movers and retired systems lost their access. Attach the signed-off recertification and the revocation evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Recertification record per data owner with each grant confirmed or rejected, and evidence that rejected grants were revoked

text.en: Record the recertification interval the organisation has chosen.
Send each data owner the current permission export for their AI data.
Collect a confirm or reject decision on every grant.
Revoke every rejected grant and keep the change record.
Check that leavers, role changes and decommissioned systems no longer hold access.

templates.title: Data stored by AI systems, including embeddings, models, logs and backups, is encrypted under managed keys
templates.description: Every persistent store of AI data is encrypted to a written standard, with keys held and rotated in a key management system, and checks confirm encryption stays on.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: CISO / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To protect stored AI datasets, embeddings, model files, logs and backups from disclosure if storage is compromised, by encrypting them under well-managed keys.
templates.successCriteria:
Every persistent store of AI data, including backups and persisted in-memory indexes, is inventoried with its encryption status.
A written standard names the approved algorithms, key lengths and key handling for each data class.
Each vector store has encryption at rest switched on, or for a managed service, documented provider encryption and key responsibility.
Keys sit in the key management system with least-privilege access and are rotated as the standard sets.
The latest verification found every inventoried store encrypted or recorded the fix.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of AI data stores with data type, classification, encryption mechanism and key reference.
Obtain the encryption standard for data at rest.
Obtain configuration exports showing encryption settings for each vector store, database, bucket and disk holding AI data, and the provider documentation for managed services.
Obtain the key management system key list, its access policy and the rotation log.
Obtain the latest verification report.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory with cloud resource listings, backup catalogues and pipeline outputs to find stores it omits, including indexes saved from in-memory libraries.
Check each store's configured algorithm and key length against the standard for its data class.
For each vector store, confirm encryption is enabled rather than merely available, and whether customer-managed keys are used where the standard requires them.
Review who can use or administer each key and whether those duties are separated, and compare rotation dates with the standard.
Inspect a sample of backups to confirm they are encrypted as well.

Output:
A store-by-store table of required against actual encryption.
A list of keys with excess access or overdue rotation.
A list of stores, including backups, found unencrypted, with the fix and its owner.

title.en: Inventory every persistent store of AI data and its encryption status

description.en: List each place AI data is written to disk: training, validation and test sets; feature sets and other intermediate files; vector databases holding embeddings; model files; platform and application logs that capture prompts or outputs; configuration files; and every backup or archive of these. Include indexes from in-memory tools that are ever saved. Record the encryption mechanism and key in use for each. Attach the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: AI data-at-rest inventory, one row per store, with data type, classification, hosting model, encryption mechanism and key reference

text.en: List the stores holding training, validation, test and intermediate data.
Add every vector database or search index holding embeddings, with its hosting model.
Add model file repositories and the logs that capture prompts, outputs or user activity.
Add configuration stores and every backup or archive of the above.
Identify in-memory indexes that are ever written to disk and add those files.
Record the encryption mechanism and key used by each store, or note that none is.

title.en: Write the encryption standard for AI data at rest by data class

description.en: Set out the algorithms, key lengths and modes the organisation approves, which encryption layer (disk, file system, database or application) applies to which kind of store, where customer-managed keys are required, and how keys are generated, held, rotated, backed up and revoked. Match the strength required to each class in the classification scheme, and make encryption the default for any new AI storage. Attach the standard.

evidenceHint.en: Encryption-at-rest standard naming approved algorithms, key lengths, layer per store type, key handling rules and the class each applies to

text.en: Record the algorithms, key lengths and modes approved for stored data.
State which encryption layer applies to each kind of AI store.
Map each classification level to the encryption and key handling it requires.
State where customer-managed keys are required rather than provider-managed ones.
Set the rotation interval and the key lifecycle steps the organisation will follow.
Require encryption to be on by default for any newly provisioned AI storage.

title.en: Turn on encryption for each vector store according to how it is hosted

description.en: For a cloud-native search or vector service, enable its built-in encryption and connect customer-managed keys where the standard requires. For a managed third-party vector database, obtain its documentation and contract terms on encryption, key responsibility and certifications, and lock down API access to it. For a self-hosted vector database, encrypt the underlying storage and secure the host. Attach the configuration or provider evidence for each.

evidenceHint.en: Per-vector-store encryption evidence: configuration export, customer-managed key binding, or provider documentation and contract clause

text.en: Enable built-in encryption on each cloud-native vector or search service.
Bind customer-managed keys to those services where the standard calls for them.
Collect encryption and key responsibility evidence from each managed vector provider.
Restrict API access to managed vector services to the identities that need it.
Encrypt the disks or file systems under each self-hosted vector database.
File the evidence against the matching inventory row.

title.en: Place AI data keys in the key management system with least-privilege access

description.en: Move or create every key protecting AI data in a hardened key management system dedicated to the purpose, and restrict who can use each key and who can administer it so that no one person holds both where the standard says they must be split. Attach the key list and access policy.

evidenceHint.en: Key management system key list for AI data with the access policy showing users and administrators per key

text.en: List every key protecting a store in the inventory.
Move any key held outside the key management system into it.
Grant use of each key only to the services and people that decrypt that store.
Separate key administration from key use where the standard requires it.
Record a backup and revocation route for each key.

title.en: Rotate AI data encryption keys on the interval the standard sets

description.en: Rotate each key protecting AI data when its interval in the standard falls due, re-encrypting or re-wrapping data as the mechanism requires, and record each rotation. Attach the rotation log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Key rotation log for the period with key identifier, date rotated and confirmation that dependent stores remained readable

text.en: List the keys whose rotation falls due in the period.
Rotate each due key in the key management system.
Re-encrypt or re-wrap the data where the mechanism needs it.
Confirm each dependent store can still be read after rotation.
Enter each rotation in the log with its date and the operator.

title.en: Verify encryption is active on every inventoried AI store and backup

description.en: Check, store by store, that encryption is switched on and matches the standard, including a sample of backups and any saved in-memory index files, and look for AI storage provisioned since the last check that bypassed the default. Attach the verification report with each gap, fix and owner.

evidenceHint.en: Verification report per store with the encryption observed, comparison with the standard, and each gap with its fix and owner

text.en: Export current encryption settings for every store in the inventory.
Compare each setting with the standard for that store's data class.
Open a sample of backups and confirm they are encrypted.
Search resource listings for AI storage created since the last check.
Record each gap with its fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: AI firewall layer placed on every AI traffic path, kept current and tested for bypass
templates.description: A dedicated firewall layer sits in front of each AI model and agent path and enforces a written policy, its rules are updated as new attack techniques appear, its events flow into security monitoring, and it is regularly tested for bypass and error rates.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: CISO / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To ensure a dedicated AI firewall layer enforces the organisation's written AI interaction policy on every path it should cover, and keeps doing so as attack techniques change.
templates.successCriteria:
A written policy states the inputs, outputs, data classes and agent actions the firewall must block, mask or allow.
Every path between users, models, agents, tools and data sources is recorded as covered by the firewall or explicitly excluded.
The latency the firewall adds on each path is measured and set against the figure the organisation accepts.
Rule and signature updates are applied and logged with dates.
Firewall alerts reach the security monitoring and incident tooling.
Bypass tests record missed threats and false blocks, each with an outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the written policy the AI firewall enforces and its approval record.
Obtain the placement record showing each AI traffic path and whether the firewall covers it, with measured added latency.
Obtain the change log of rule and threat-signature updates for the period.
Obtain the integration configuration forwarding firewall events to the security monitoring and incident response tools, and a sample of alerts received there.
Obtain the latest bypass test report.

Analysis:
Trace each policy statement to at least one firewall rule and list policy statements with no rule.
Compare the placement record with the current architecture and name any AI path, including agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent traffic, that bypasses the firewall.
Compare measured latency with the figure the organisation accepts.
Check the change log for gaps where new threat information was available but no update was applied.
Confirm sampled alerts arrived in the monitoring tool and were handled.
Review the bypass report for missed threats and false blocks and confirm each has an outcome.

Output:
A policy-to-rule coverage table.
A list of uncovered AI paths and paths over their latency figure.
A list of bypasses and false blocks with the outcome recorded for each.

title.en: Write the policy of inputs, outputs and agent actions the AI firewall must stop

description.en: Before configuring the firewall, set out in one document what counts as unacceptable input, which data classes must never appear in output, what content must be blocked, and which tool calls and data reads agents may not make through it. Agree it with the owners of the AI systems it will protect. Attach the signed-off policy; the firewall's configuration is derived from it.

evidenceHint.en: Approved AI firewall policy listing barred input types, protected data classes, blocked content and disallowed agent actions

text.en: List the input types to be blocked or cleaned, such as injection attempts.
Name the data classes the firewall must stop from leaving in a model reply.
Define the harmful or out-of-scope content categories to be blocked.
State the agent tool calls and data reads the firewall must refuse.
Record sign-off from the owner of each AI system the policy covers.

title.en: Record where the AI firewall intercepts each model, agent and tool path

description.en: Decide and document the inspection point for each AI traffic path: at the network edge, at the API gateway, between the application and the model, or inside the agent framework for agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent calls. Measure the latency the firewall adds on each path and compare it with the figure the organisation is willing to accept. Attach the placement record with the measurements.

evidenceHint.en: Placement record per AI traffic path naming the inspection point, or the reason it is excluded, and the measured added latency

text.en: List every path between users, models, agents, tools and data sources.
Choose the inspection point for each path and the firewall component that serves it.
Write down the reason for any path the firewall deliberately does not cover.
Measure response time on each path with and without the firewall in line.
Record the latency figure you accept and flag paths that exceed it.

title.en: Route AI firewall events and alerts into security monitoring and incident tooling

description.en: Send the firewall's logs of inspected traffic, detections and actions to the event correlation platform, raise real-time alerts for the event types the policy marks as critical, and connect those alerts to the automated response or ticketing route the security team already uses. Attach the integration configuration and an example alert received end to end.

evidenceHint.en: Integration configuration for log and alert forwarding, plus one test alert traced from firewall to incident ticket

text.en: Configure the firewall to export detection and action logs to the correlation platform.
Define which event types page the security team at once rather than wait for review.
Link those alerts to the existing automated response or ticketing workflow.
Generate a test detection and confirm it arrives as a ticket.

title.en: Apply AI firewall rule and threat-signature updates and log each change

description.en: As new prompt injection techniques, malicious indicators and leakage patterns are published by threat intelligence feeds or found in your own logs, update the firewall's rules, signatures and any guardian model. Log every change with its date, its trigger and who made it, and note any change that alters what the policy says. Attach the change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: AI firewall change log for the period, one row per rule, signature or guardian model update with date, trigger and author

text.en: Check subscribed threat intelligence feeds for new AI attack techniques.
Add or adjust rules and signatures to cover each relevant new technique.
Update or retrain the guardian model where its vendor or team issues a new version.
Enter each change in the log with date, trigger and the person who applied it.

title.en: Run bypass tests against the AI firewall and record missed threats and false blocks

description.en: Attempt to get past the firewall with current evasion techniques on every covered path, and replay a set of legitimate but unusual complex queries to see what it wrongly stops. Record the missed threats and false blocks, decide for each whether to tune a rule, add a control or accept the result, and compare the rates with the previous test. Attach the test report.

evidenceHint.en: Bypass test report per covered path listing missed threats, false blocks and the outcome decided for each

text.en: Assemble evasion attempts reflecting techniques published since the last test.
Run them against each covered path, including agent-to-tool traffic.
Replay legitimate complex queries and note any the firewall blocks in error.
Record the outcome for each miss or false block: tune, add a control, or accept.
Compare miss and false-block rates with the previous test report.

templates.title: Each agent reaches only the tools, APIs and data its function needs
templates.description: Every agent has a versioned privilege set justified by its function, an enforcement point the agent cannot bypass refuses any call outside that set, and temporary widening is approved by a person and withdrawn when the task ends.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / CISO
templates.objective: To limit what any agent can do to the tools, APIs and data its designated function requires, so that a misled or compromised agent cannot act beyond that scope.
templates.successCriteria:
Every agent in production appears in the privilege matrix with its function, each permitted tool, endpoint and data source, and a business reason for each grant.
Calls outside an agent's matrix entry are refused at the mediation layer or operating system and logged with the agent's identity.
Each temporary privilege increase in the period has a recorded human approval and a recorded withdrawal.
Grants unused in the review period were removed or kept with a written reason.
Attempts to reach an unlisted tool, including through a shell or alternative path, were refused in testing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the agent privilege matrix with its version history and the business reason recorded for each grant.
Obtain the authorisation policy loaded into the tool-mediation layer or API gateway, and any operating-system allow-lists for agents able to run commands.
Obtain the log of refused agent calls and the log of temporary privilege requests, approvals and withdrawals for the period.
Obtain the latest privilege review record and the results of bypass testing.

Analysis:
Compare the list of agents deployed in production with the matrix and note any agent missing from it.
Compare the enforced policy with the matrix, grant by grant, and note grants that are enforced but undocumented or documented but unenforced.
For a sample of refused calls, confirm the agent identity, requested operation and reason were recorded.
Match every temporary privilege increase to an approval and to its withdrawal.
Compare each agent's grants with its logged use over the period and identify grants never exercised.
Read the bypass test results for any route that reached a tool outside the matrix.

Output:
A table of agents showing matrix coverage and any mismatch between documented and enforced grants.
A list of escalations lacking approval or withdrawal, unused grants still in place, and any bypass that succeeded.

title.en: Record a privilege matrix of the tools, APIs and data each agent type may use

description.en: For each agent type, write down its business function and the exact APIs, endpoints, tools and data sources it needs for that function, marking whether each grant reads, writes or executes, with a business reason per grant. Keep the matrix under version control so every change is traceable. Attach the matrix and the reference of the version in force.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned agent privilege matrix, one row per agent type and grant, with the access mode and business reason for each

text.en: List every agent type in use and the business function each is meant to perform.
Name each API endpoint, tool and data source the function requires, nothing more.
Mark each grant as read, write or execute and state why the function needs it.
Record any contextual limits you apply, such as transaction value, time window or jurisdiction, with the values you chose.
Commit the matrix to version control and note the commit or version reference.

title.en: Configure the tool-mediation layer to refuse calls outside each agent's matrix entry

description.en: The component that turns an agent's request into a real API or tool call is where authorisation must be checked, because a rule held only in the prompt is advice the agent can ignore. Load the matrix as the policy there, check the calling agent's identity and the requested operation and parameters against it before any call is made, and log every refusal. Attach the policy configuration and a sample refusal log entry.

evidenceHint.en: Tool-mediation or API gateway authorisation configuration derived from the matrix, with a sample refusal log entry showing agent identity and requested operation

text.en: Identify the mediation layer or gateway every agent tool call passes through.
Translate each matrix entry into an allow rule there and deny everything not named.
Check the requested endpoint and parameter values against the agent's allowed scope before execution.
Log each refused call with the agent identity, the operation asked for and the reason.
Remove generic capabilities such as raw HTTP or a shell where they would bypass narrower governed tools.

title.en: Configure operating-system execution limits for agents that can run commands

description.en: An agent able to start programs can step around the gateway, so put an enforcement point beneath it that the agent cannot change. Give it a deny-by-default list of executables named by absolute path, each with an argument schema, never interpreters or program launchers, and run anything general-purpose as a short-lived sandboxed job with no credentials and default-deny network. Attach the allow-list, the argument schemas and the sandbox configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Executable allow-list with argument schemas, environment allow-list and sandboxed-job configuration for each command-running agent

text.en: List the agents able to launch programs or open a shell in any environment.
Write each permitted program as an absolute path with a schema for its arguments and values.
Exclude shells, interpreters and options that accept a script or another program to run.
Pin each permitted executable by hash on storage the agent cannot write to.
Build each command's environment variables from an allow-list instead of inheriting the agent's.
Send builds, test runs and code the model wrote to sandboxed jobs with no credentials and no default network.

title.en: Log each temporary privilege increase from approval through to its withdrawal

description.en: When an agent needs access beyond its matrix entry for a task, the increase must be approved by a person, limited to a stated period or task, and taken away automatically when that ends. Record each request, who approved it, the scope granted and when it was withdrawn, and send these records to the security monitoring system. The approval mechanism itself is defined under the human approval gate mitigation. Attach the escalation log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Privilege escalation log for the period, each entry showing the agent, scope, approver, expiry condition and withdrawal time

text.en: Record each escalation request with the agent, the extra access asked for and the task it serves.
Attach the human approval or refusal to the request before any access is granted.
Set the expiry condition, a time or task completion, on every approved increase.
Confirm the extra access was removed when the condition was met and log the time.
Forward escalation and withdrawal events to the security monitoring system.

title.en: Reconcile each agent's granted privileges against the calls it actually made

description.en: At the review interval you have set, export each agent's current grants and compare them with its logged calls over the period, so access the function no longer needs can be removed. Also look for usage patterns that suggest abuse or compromise. Keep a grant that went unused only with a written reason. Attach the reconciliation, the grants removed and the updated matrix version.

evidenceHint.en: Per-agent reconciliation of granted against exercised privileges, listing grants removed, grants retained with reasons and the new matrix version

text.en: Export the grants currently enforced for each agent from the mediation layer.
Pull each agent's call log for the period and list the grants it exercised.
Mark grants never exercised and decide for each whether to remove or retain it.
Flag call patterns that depart from the agent's usual behaviour for investigation.
Update the matrix with the removals and record the new version reference.

title.en: Test whether an agent can reach a tool or API outside its matrix entry

description.en: Try, for each agent, to call tools and endpoints it is not granted: directly through the mediation layer, through any alternative route such as a shell or another tool reaching the same system, and with argument variations on a permitted command that would widen its effect. Every attempt should be refused and logged. Attach the test plan, the results and the remediation for any success.

evidenceHint.en: Bypass test results per agent, showing each attempt, whether it was refused and logged, and remediation for any that succeeded

text.en: Pick, for each agent, endpoints and tools its matrix entry does not grant.
Request each one through the mediation layer and record the outcome.
Try the same effect through alternative routes such as a shell, raw HTTP or another tool.
Vary the arguments of a permitted command to see whether its reach can be widened.
Check that every refused attempt appears in the refusal log with the agent's identity.

templates.title: Agent tool calls checked for fitness, parameters and sequence before they execute
templates.description: Every tool call an agent makes passes a runtime check of whether that tool fits the task and caller, whether its parameters satisfy declared schemas and business rules, and whether the call order matches an approved pattern; failures are blocked and reported to security monitoring.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Engineering Lead / Security Engineering Lead
templates.objective: To prevent a manipulated agent from choosing an unsuitable tool, passing harmful parameters to an API or chaining calls into an unapproved workflow at the moment of execution.
templates.successCriteria:
Each agent tool is mapped to the task categories it may serve, and high-risk tools carry a declared parameter schema with business rule checks.
A validation layer in front of tool execution checks tool choice, parameters and call order on every call and blocks failures.
Output from one tool is sanitised before it is passed as input to the next.
Validation failures appear in security monitoring, and repeated failures by one agent are escalated.
Rule changes are version controlled and tested outside production before release.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the task-to-tool mapping and the parameter schemas and business rules defined for each high-risk tool.
Obtain the configuration of the validation layer that sits in front of tool execution, and the approved call sequence patterns it enforces.
Obtain validation event logs for the period and the security monitoring records they fed.
Obtain the version history of the validation rules and the test results recorded for each change.

Analysis:
Select a sample of agent tools and confirm each has a mapping entry and, if high risk, a schema covering type, format, range and business rules.
In a non-production environment, submit calls with an unmapped tool, an out-of-range value, an injection string aimed at a database, shell or interpreter, and a forbidden call order, and confirm each is blocked and logged.
Pass a crafted output from one tool into the next and confirm it is cleaned before use.
Trace a sample of logged validation failures into the monitoring system and confirm repeated failures produced an escalation.
Compare rule changes in the period with their recorded test results.

Output:
A per-tool table of mapping, schema and test outcome, naming tools that are unvalidated or let a bad call through.
A list of validation failures that never reached monitoring or were not escalated.
A list of rule changes released without a recorded test.

title.en: Map each agent tool to the task categories it may be selected for

description.en: For every tool an agent can call, record the task categories it is suitable for, whether it only reads or can change data or move value, and the caller authority it presupposes, so that a runtime check can refuse a tool chosen for the wrong job. This control checks the fit of each call; which tools an agent is granted at all is set under least privilege (MI-18). Attach the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Task-to-tool mapping, one row per tool, giving permitted task categories, read or write nature and required caller authority

text.en: Export the list of tools each agent can reach from its configuration or tool manager.
Classify each tool as read-only or able to change records, send messages or move value.
Record the task categories for which each tool is an appropriate choice.
Record the caller authority, such as user role or transaction value, each tool presupposes.
Flag the tools whose misuse would cause the most harm as high risk for schema work.

title.en: Define parameter schemas and business rules for every high-risk agent tool

description.en: For each tool flagged high risk, write the schema its parameters must satisfy: data types, formats, permitted ranges, allowed values for identifiers, amounts and codes, rules on which parameters may appear together, and the business limits that apply. Note which parameters reach a database query, operating system command or code interpreter downstream and the sanitisation each needs. Attach the schemas in the repository where the validation layer reads them.

evidenceHint.en: Version-controlled parameter schemas for high-risk tools, covering types, formats, ranges, allowed values, combination rules and business limits

text.en: Write the type, format and range constraint for every parameter of each high-risk tool.
List the permitted values for account identifiers, amounts and authorisation codes.
Write the rules that reject parameter combinations which make no business sense.
Mark parameters that flow into SQL, shell commands or interpreters and name their escaping.
Commit the schemas to version control with the reviewer named on the change.

title.en: Configure pre-execution validation of tool choice, parameters and call order in the tool manager

description.en: Place a validation step at the point where the agent's tool manager or API gateway executes calls. It checks the chosen tool against the mapping and caller authority, the parameters against the schemas, the output of a prior tool before it becomes the next tool's input, and the call order against the approved workflow patterns and any forbidden pairings. Where a pattern requires a person to approve before continuing, the step hands off to the approval gate owned by MI-24. Attach the configuration and the list of patterns enforced.

evidenceHint.en: Validation layer configuration and the approved call sequence patterns and forbidden pairings it enforces

text.en: Route every agent tool call through one validation step before it reaches the target API.
Reject calls whose tool falls outside the mapping for the task or the caller's authority.
Reject calls whose parameters fail the tool's schema or business rules.
Clean each tool's output before the agent may pass it as input to another tool.
Encode the approved call sequences and forbidden pairings and block anything outside them.
Configure the step to emit an event for every rejection with tool, agent and reason.

title.en: Route tool validation failures to security monitoring and escalate repeat offenders

description.en: Send every validation rejection to the security monitoring system with the agent, tool, rule broken and session, and set an escalation when the same agent or session keeps failing. Triage each alert and record whether it was an attack, a misconfigured rule or a false positive. Attach the alert log and triage outcomes for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Validation alert log for the period with each alert's triage outcome and any escalations raised

text.en: Ship validation rejection events to the security monitoring system with agent and tool.
Set the repeat-failure count and window that trigger an escalation, and record your choice.
Triage each alert as attempted manipulation, rule defect or legitimate call blocked.
Open a rule change for each false positive that blocked legitimate agent work.
Pass suspected manipulation cases to incident response with the full call chain.

title.en: Test validation rules with injected parameters and forbidden sequences before each release

description.en: Before a rule change or new tool reaches production, run a test set in a non-production environment that tries unmapped tools, out-of-range and malformed values, injection strings aimed at databases, shells and interpreters, tainted tool outputs and forbidden call orders. Record which were blocked. Periodically compare the rule set with current tools, business processes and threat reports to find gaps. Attach the test results and coverage notes.

evidenceHint.en: Pre-release test results for validation rule changes and a coverage note listing tools or patterns without rules

text.en: Keep a test set of malicious parameters, unmapped tools and forbidden call orders.
Run the test set in a non-production environment against every rule change or new tool.
Record each case as blocked or passed and fix any rule that let a bad call through.
Compare the rules with current tools, workflows and threat reports to find gaps.
File the results against the version of the rules that was released.

templates.title: Only vetted, approved MCP servers can be connected to agents, and their behaviour is watched
templates.description: Agents reach MCP servers only through an enforced allowlist of servers that were vetted before approval, over authenticated encrypted connections, with server behaviour monitored and a rehearsed procedure for cutting off a compromised server.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of Security Engineering / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To prevent agents from relying on an MCP server that has not been vetted, approved and monitored, so a compromised server cannot steer agent decisions or receive data.
templates.successCriteria:
Every MCP server in use is in an inventory naming its operator, approved version and the protection tier the organisation chose.
Each approved server has a vetting record: code or vendor review, dependency and licence scan, and vulnerability check.
Clients reach MCP servers only through an enforced allowlist over authenticated, encrypted connections.
Server connections and responses are logged with the calling user or agent and monitored for anomalies.
A procedure for isolating a compromised server has been exercised, and approved servers are re-reviewed at the interval set.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the MCP server inventory with approved versions and the protection tier recorded for each deployment.
Obtain the vetting record for each approved server.
Obtain the proxy or gateway allowlist configuration and the client configuration that forces connections through it.
Obtain connection logs and monitoring alerts for the period, and the subscription to advisories for the server software.
Obtain the isolation procedure, the record of its last exercise, and the re-review records for approved servers.

Analysis:
Confirm every inventoried server has a vetting record dated before it was first allowed, and that the version running matches the version vetted.
From a managed client, attempt a direct connection to an MCP server not on the allowlist and confirm it fails.
Inspect a sample of connections for encryption and authentication of both ends where the chosen tier requires it.
Compare servers seen in connection logs with the allowlist and list any outside it.
Trace a sample of anomaly alerts and advisories to their handling.
Check that each approved server was re-reviewed within the interval the organisation set.

Output:
A server-by-server table of vetting, version match, connection protection and last re-review.
A list of connections to unapproved servers and of bypasses of the allowlist.
Findings from the isolation exercise with the actions agreed.

title.en: Inventory every MCP server agents connect to, with its operator, version and chosen protection tier

description.en: List each MCP server any agent, coding assistant or workflow connects to, whether it is open source or commercial, who operates it, the implementation version in use, the data and actions it exposes, and the tier of governance the organisation has chosen for that deployment, from a centrally proxied set with human approval of actions up to fully monitored many-to-many use. Attach the inventory with its date.

evidenceHint.en: MCP server inventory, one row per server, naming operator, version, exposed data and actions, and the governance tier chosen

text.en: Collect MCP server entries from agent, assistant and developer tool configurations.
Record for each server whether it is open source or commercial and who runs it.
Record the implementation version currently in use for every server.
Describe the data each server supplies and the actions it lets an agent take.
Record the governance tier you chose for each deployment and the reason for that choice.

title.en: Assess each MCP server before it is added to the approved list

description.en: Before approval, review an open source server's code and a commercial provider's security posture, scan the server's dependencies including transitive ones for known vulnerabilities and licence problems, and record the outcome against the exact version reviewed. For a commercial provider, record the certifications, penetration test results and architecture information obtained. Contract terms with the provider sit under MI-7. Attach the vetting record and the approval decision.

evidenceHint.en: Vetting record per MCP server version: code or vendor review, dependency and licence scan, vulnerability results and approval decision

text.en: Review the source of an open source server for data handling and unexpected network calls.
Scan direct and transitive dependencies for known vulnerabilities and licence conflicts.
Obtain certifications, test reports and architecture details from a commercial provider.
Record the exact version reviewed and the reviewer's decision with any conditions.
Add the server to the allowlist only after the approval decision is filed.

title.en: Configure the MCP proxy to admit only allowlisted servers over authenticated encrypted connections

description.en: Route all MCP client traffic through a centrally administered proxy or gateway that permits connections only to the approved servers and versions, and configure clients so they cannot connect around it. Require encryption on every connection and authenticate the server, and both ends where the chosen tier calls for it. Propagate the calling user or agent identity through the proxy for the audit trail. Attach the configuration and a test showing a blocked direct connection.

evidenceHint.en: Proxy allowlist and encryption configuration, client settings forcing use of the proxy, and a test record of a blocked direct connection

text.en: Load the approved servers and versions into the proxy allowlist from the vetting records.
Set managed client configuration so MCP connections can only go through the proxy.
Require encrypted transport and certificate validation for every proxied connection.
Enable mutual authentication for the deployments whose tier requires it.
Pass the calling user or agent identity through the proxy into its connection log.
Attempt a direct connection to an unlisted server and file the refusal as evidence.

title.en: Monitor MCP server connections, responses and security advisories for signs of compromise

description.en: Watch proxy logs for connections to unexpected servers, shifts in response size, error rates or content that depart from a server's normal pattern, and responses that fail schema checks, and subscribe to advisories for every approved server's software. Investigate each alert and record the outcome. Attach the alert and advisory log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Log of MCP monitoring alerts and security advisories for the period, with the investigation outcome for each

text.en: Alert on any proxied connection attempt to a server outside the allowlist.
Alert when a server's response pattern, error rate or availability departs from its norm.
Subscribe to vulnerability advisories for each approved server and its dependencies.
Record the investigation and outcome for every alert and relevant advisory.
Remove or suspend a server from the allowlist when an investigation finds it unsafe.

title.en: Exercise the procedure for cutting off a compromised MCP server

description.en: Write and rehearse the steps for removing a suspect server from the allowlist, keeping agents working in a reduced mode without it, preserving connection and response logs for forensic review, checking data the server supplied before the cut-off, and restoring the connection only after renewed vetting. Run the exercise against one approved server and record timings and gaps. Attach the procedure and the exercise report.

evidenceHint.en: MCP server isolation procedure and the report of its most recent exercise, with timings, gaps found and actions

text.en: Document how a server is removed from the allowlist and who may authorise it.
Document how agents degrade or fall back when that server is unavailable.
Document which logs are preserved and how supplied data is rechecked after a cut-off.
Run the procedure against one approved server and time each step.
Record the gaps found and assign an owner to each remediation.

title.en: Reassess approved MCP servers and reconcile the allowlist with servers seen in use

description.en: At the interval the organisation sets, re-run the vetting for each approved server against the version now running, and compare servers seen in proxy logs and client configurations with the allowlist. Remove servers no longer needed. Attach the re-review records and the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Re-review record per approved MCP server and a reconciliation of the allowlist with servers seen in use

text.en: Record the re-review interval you set for approved MCP servers.
Compare the version each server runs with the version recorded at approval.
Repeat the dependency and vulnerability scan for any server whose version changed.
List servers seen in logs or configurations that the allowlist does not contain.
Remove allowlist entries for servers no team still uses and note the date.

templates.title: A compromised or failing agent cannot reach, influence or take down the agents around it
templates.description: Each agent runs in its own compartment with segregated state and storage, inter-agent traffic is authenticated and limited to approved routes, and a misbehaving agent can be cut off while the rest continue.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / Infrastructure Security Lead
templates.objective: To contain the effect of one agent's compromise or malfunction within that agent, so that it cannot move laterally or cascade across a multi-agent workflow.
templates.successCriteria:
Every agent in a multi-agent system has a recorded trust level, and the boundaries between levels are documented with their rationale.
Each agent type runs in its own container, VM or account with its own state store, cache and temporary storage.
Inter-agent messages use mutual authentication and follow only routes in the communication matrix, and each exchange is logged.
A failing agent can be isolated while dependent workflows continue in a reduced form.
The latest isolation test found no cross-agent access, or each finding has a fix.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the agent classification with trust levels and the documented trust boundaries.
Obtain the deployment configuration for each agent: container or VM, runtime account, resource limits, state store, cache and temporary storage.
Obtain the inter-agent communication matrix, the channel authentication configuration and the cross-agent interaction log for the period.
Obtain the circuit-breaker configuration, the record of isolation events and the latest isolation or penetration test report.

Analysis:
Compare the agents in production with the classification and note any agent without a trust level.
Check from the deployment configuration that no two agent types share a runtime account, state store, cache or temporary area.
Compare logged inter-agent exchanges with the matrix and identify any route or message type it does not allow.
Confirm each channel requires both parties to authenticate and encrypts traffic in transit.
For each isolation event, confirm the agent was cut off and the effect on other agents was recorded.
Read the test report for any successful cross-agent read, message or privilege gain.

Output:
A table of agents showing trust level, compartment and any shared resource found.
A list of exchanges outside the matrix, unauthenticated channels, and open isolation test findings with owners.

title.en: Classify every agent by trust level and record the boundaries between levels

description.en: For each multi-agent system, list its agents and assign each a trust level according to how sensitive the data it handles is, the authority it holds and its risk profile. Then write down which levels may interact, what crosses each boundary and why the line sits where it does. Attach the classification and the boundary document.

evidenceHint.en: Agent classification register with trust level per agent, and the trust-boundary document with rationale for each boundary

text.en: List every agent in each multi-agent system with the workflow it belongs to.
Rate each agent on data sensitivity, authority held and risk profile.
Assign each agent a trust level from the scale you define and record the scale.
Write down which trust levels may interact and the data classes allowed across each boundary.
Record the reasoning behind each boundary so later changes can be judged against it.

title.en: Record the communication matrix of which agents may message which, and with what data

description.en: Draw up the allowed routes between agents: for each pair that needs to interact, the direction, the message types and data formats permitted, and any interaction that crosses a trust boundary and so needs extra approval. Anything not listed is refused. Attach the matrix with its version reference.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned inter-agent communication matrix listing permitted pairs, direction, message types and cross-boundary approvals

text.en: List each pair of agents that must exchange messages for the workflow to function.
Record the direction and the message types and formats each pair may exchange.
Mark routes that cross a trust boundary and the approval each one needs.
State that every route not listed is denied by default.
Version the matrix and note who approved it.

title.en: Deploy each agent type in its own container or VM with separate state, cache and temporary storage

description.en: Run each agent type under its own runtime account in its own container or virtual machine, with resource limits, its own database instance or schema, its own cache and its own temporary area cleaned up after use, so one agent cannot read or corrupt another's working data. Use hypervisor-level separation for the agents you classed as most critical. Attach the deployment configuration for each agent type.

evidenceHint.en: Deployment configuration per agent type showing compartment, runtime account, resource limits, state store, cache and temporary storage

text.en: Place each agent type in a separate container, or a separate VM for critical agents.
Run each agent type under its own operating-system account with minimal rights.
Set CPU, memory and storage limits on each agent's compartment.
Give each agent type its own database instance or schema with access limited to that agent.
Provide separate cache and temporary storage per agent and clean temporary data after each task.
Use a distinct service account per agent type for each external service it calls.

title.en: Configure mutual authentication and route enforcement on every inter-agent channel

description.en: Every channel between agents must have both ends prove their identity, encrypt traffic, and refuse any route or message type the communication matrix does not allow. Log each exchange so cross-agent interactions can be monitored and investigated. Attach the channel configuration and a sample of the interaction log.

evidenceHint.en: Inter-agent channel configuration showing mutual authentication, encryption and matrix enforcement, plus a sample of the cross-agent interaction log

text.en: Issue each agent a certificate or token used to authenticate it to other agents.
Require both sides of every inter-agent connection to authenticate before data is exchanged.
Encrypt inter-agent traffic in transit and add encryption of individual messages that carry sensitive data.
Enforce the communication matrix at the channel and reject unlisted routes and message types.
Log every exchange with sender, receiver, message type and time.

title.en: Disable a misbehaving agent through its circuit breaker and record the containment

description.en: Set a circuit breaker on each agent so that when health checks fail, behaviour looks anomalous or a boundary violation is detected, the agent is isolated and the workflow continues with reduced capability. Each time it trips, record what triggered it, what was isolated, how dependent agents were affected and how the agent was safely restored. Attach the isolation event log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Agent isolation event log, each entry showing trigger, agent isolated, effect on other agents and restoration steps

text.en: Configure the conditions that trip each agent's circuit breaker and record them.
Define the reduced mode each dependent workflow falls back to when an agent is isolated.
Log each trip with the trigger, the agent isolated and the time.
Record how other agents were affected while the agent was cut off.
Record the checks made before the isolated agent was returned to service.

title.en: Test the isolation boundaries between agents with a penetration test

description.en: Attempt, from inside one agent's compartment, to read another agent's state, cache or temporary files, to send messages along routes the matrix forbids, to reach another agent's network, and to gain authority by working through a higher-trust agent. Record every attempt and its result, and track any that succeeded to a fix. Attach the test report.

evidenceHint.en: Isolation penetration test report listing each cross-agent attempt, its result and the remediation for any success

text.en: From one agent's compartment, try to read another agent's state store, cache and temporary files.
Send messages on routes and with message types the matrix does not allow.
Try to reach another agent's network endpoints outside an approved channel.
Attempt to gain authority by passing requests through a higher-trust agent.
Record each result and open a remediation item for every successful attempt.

templates.title: Agents hold no standing secrets and cannot discover the credentials around them
templates.description: Agent environments carry no embedded secrets, agents receive short-lived task-scoped credentials from a broker that verifies them, secret stores are unreachable from agent networks, and credential-hunting behaviour raises an alert.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: CISO / Identity and Access Management Lead
templates.objective: To stop agents from finding, holding or exfiltrating credentials, so that a compromised agent cannot harvest secrets to move into other systems.
templates.successCriteria:
A scan of each agent image, environment and reachable file system finds no embedded credentials.
Agents obtain credentials only from a broker that authenticates them and issues task-scoped credentials that expire.
Agent networks cannot reach secret stores, credential administration APIs or metadata services, and credential-revealing tools are denied.
Credential-discovery behaviour by an agent raises an alert, and each alert has a recorded outcome.
Emergency rotation of credentials exposed to an agent has been rehearsed and its gaps recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of credentials agents use or can reach, and secret-scan results for each agent image and environment.
Obtain the credential broker configuration showing authentication of agents, scoping and expiry of issued credentials.
Obtain the network and tool restrictions applied to agent environments, covering secret stores, credential APIs, metadata services and administration tools.
Obtain the detection rules for credential discovery, the alerts raised in the period with their outcomes, and the last rotation exercise record.

Analysis:
Re-run or sample the secret scan and confirm no credential appears in an agent image, variable or file.
Trace a sample of agent credentials to the broker and confirm each was scoped to a task and expired.
From an agent environment, test whether secret stores, credential APIs and metadata endpoints answer.
Compare the detection rules with the discovery techniques the organisation identified and note any not covered.
Check each alert for a recorded disposition and each exercise for the related credentials it rotated.

Output:
A list of embedded or standing credentials found in agent environments.
A statement of which credential stores and tools agents could reach, alerts without a disposition, and gaps from the rotation exercise.

title.en: Inventory every credential an agent uses or could reach from its environment

description.en: Look beyond the keys an agent is meant to use. Scan agent images, environment variables, configuration files, mounted volumes and logs for secrets, and list the secret stores, credential APIs and metadata services reachable from the agent's network. Record each credential's location, what it unlocks and whether the agent needs it. Attach the inventory and the scan output.

evidenceHint.en: Agent credential inventory, one row per credential with location, what it grants and whether needed, plus the secret-scan output

text.en: List the credentials each agent legitimately uses and the systems they unlock.
Scan each agent image, environment variable set and configuration file for secrets.
Check mounted volumes, logs, core dumps and swap areas reachable by agents for stored secrets.
List the secret stores, credential APIs and metadata services reachable from agent networks.
Mark each credential found as needed by the agent or to be removed.

title.en: Remove embedded secrets from agent images, environment variables and file systems

description.en: Rebuild agent images and environments so they carry no keys, tokens, certificates or configuration files with secrets in them, and stop agents reading process environment variables that might carry credentials. Re-run the secret scan on the rebuilt images to show they are clean. Attach the before and after scan results.

evidenceHint.en: Secret-scan results for each agent image and environment before and after removal, showing no remaining credentials

text.en: Delete credentials and secret-bearing configuration files from each agent image build.
Strip credentials from the environment variables passed into agent processes.
Remove credential files from file systems the agent can read.
Rebuild and redeploy the cleaned images.
Re-run the secret scan on the redeployed images and file the results.

title.en: Configure a credential broker that issues agents short-lived, task-scoped credentials

description.en: Put a broker between agents and the credential vault. It verifies which agent is asking and whether the request fits that agent's authorised function, then issues a credential limited to the task, resource and time window, ideally injected at a gateway so the agent never sees it, and lets it expire when the task or session ends. Keep the vault in a network segment agents cannot reach. Attach the broker configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Credential broker configuration showing agent authentication, request validation, credential scope and expiry, and the vault's network placement

text.en: Place the credential vault in a network segment with no route from agent environments.
Require the broker to authenticate the requesting agent before issuing anything.
Check each request against the agent's authorised function before a credential is issued.
Limit each issued credential to one task, resource set and time window.
Inject credentials at the gateway where possible so the agent never handles the value.
Expire credentials automatically when the task or session ends.

title.en: Restrict agent access to secret stores, credential administration APIs and credential-revealing tools

description.en: Deny agent environments network routes and name resolution to secret stores and authentication infrastructure, block cloud and infrastructure APIs and metadata services that can return credentials, and refuse agents the process viewers, memory analysers and administration functions that could expose secrets. Attach the network rules and tool restrictions in force.

evidenceHint.en: Network deny rules, DNS restrictions and tool deny lists applied to agent environments, covering secret stores, credential APIs and metadata services

text.en: Add network rules denying agent segments any route to secret stores and authentication services.
Block name resolution for credential management hosts from agent environments.
Deny agent calls to credential management, cloud management and instance metadata endpoints.
Remove process viewers, memory analysers and database administration functions from agent tool sets.
Deny agent file access to configuration directories where credentials are usually kept.

title.en: Detect agent behaviour that looks like credential discovery and raise an alert

description.en: Set a baseline of how each agent normally requests and uses credentials, then alert on departures from it: repeated credential requests, reads of configuration files, logs, core dumps or swap, queries probing for stored secrets, and use of administration tools. Send these events to the security monitoring system and record what was done about each alert. Attach the alert log with dispositions for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Credential-discovery alert log for the period, each alert with the agent, the behaviour detected and its disposition

text.en: Record each agent's normal pattern of credential requests and use as a baseline.
Create detections for reads of configuration files, core dumps and swap by agents.
Create detections for repeated or enumerating credential requests across systems.
Forward credential-related agent events to the security monitoring system.
Record the investigation outcome against every alert raised.

title.en: Exercise emergency rotation and revocation of credentials exposed to a compromised agent

description.en: Run an exercise in which an agent is assumed compromised: identify every credential it held or could have reached, including related ones that would also need changing, rotate and revoke them across all systems, and use the audit trail of credential access to judge what was exposed. Record the time taken and every gap found. Attach the exercise record.

evidenceHint.en: Rotation exercise record listing credentials identified, rotated and revoked, time taken, and gaps with owners

text.en: Choose an agent and assume it has been compromised for the exercise.
List every credential it held or could reach, using the inventory and access trail.
Identify related credentials that would also need rotating if those were exposed.
Rotate and revoke the listed credentials across every system that accepts them.
Record the time each step took and every gap, with an owner for each fix.

templates.title: Designated high-impact agent actions wait for an authorised person's decision on the exact action
templates.description: Actions the organisation has designated as high impact are suspended before any side effect and released only when an authorised, independent approver decides on the fully resolved action, with the decision recorded against it.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of Operational Risk / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To make sure an agent cannot carry out an action the organisation has designated as high impact until an authorised person has decided on that exact action.
templates.successCriteria:
A versioned policy lists every action class needing approval, its trigger and approver tier.
Gated actions are suspended at the tool-mediation layer before any side effect, and no unmediated path reaches the same effect.
Each approval is bound to the resolved action's digest, was made by an authorised person other than the requester, and is recorded.
Every standing pre-approval records grantor, scope, environment and expiry, and actions released under it are linked to it.
Testing found no way to execute, alter or repeat a gated action without a valid approval.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approval policy with its version history, listing gated action classes, triggers and approver tiers.
Obtain the gate configuration in the tool-mediation layer, the inventory of alternative action paths and the state model for pending actions.
Obtain the approval records for the period, the register of standing pre-approvals, and the gate hit-rate and rejection-rate figures.
Obtain the latest adversarial test results for the gate.

Analysis:
Sample executed actions in designated classes and confirm each has an approval or a linked standing grant.
For sampled approvals, compare the approved digest with the executed action and check the approver held authority for that tier.
Confirm no approver in the sample was the requester or acted through a shared account.
Check each standing grant was made by someone with authority and has a scope, environment and expiry.
Compare approval rates and backlog with the thresholds and look for signs of rubber-stamping.
Read the test results for any execution without approval, self-approval, repeat or altered parameters.

Output:
A list of designated actions executed without a matching approval or grant, and approvals made without authority.
A statement of standing grants lacking scope or expiry, gate metrics of concern and open test findings.

title.en: Record the agent action classes that require human approval and what triggers each

description.en: Judge candidate actions by their worst-case impact on confidentiality, integrity, money, customers, legal position and external disclosure, treating reversibility as one factor rather than an exemption. For each class you designate, record the trigger, such as a value or aggregate limit you choose or a sensitive counterparty, the approver tier drawn from your delegated authorities, and limits that must be refused outright rather than escalated. Attach the versioned policy.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned approval policy listing each gated action class, its trigger and chosen threshold, approver tier and any non-waivable limit

text.en: List the agent actions that could cause material financial, customer, legal or disclosure harm.
Assess each against the impact dimensions and note reversibility as a factor.
Record the trigger for each designated class with the threshold value you set.
Name the approver tier for each class from your delegated-authority framework.
Mark limits that must be denied outright instead of routed for approval.
Version the policy and state whether a policy change voids pending approvals.

title.en: Configure the gate to suspend designated actions before any side effect is issued

description.en: Check the approval policy in the layer that carries out the agent's tool and API calls, and make sure agents cannot reach the same effect another way. Hold each designated action as a minimal encrypted record, without reusable credentials, bind any approval to a digest of the fully resolved action with a validity period, re-check changing conditions just before release, and use an idempotency key, or park an ambiguous result as outcome-unknown for a person, so a crash never causes a silent repeat. Attach the configuration and the state model.

evidenceHint.en: Gate configuration in the tool-mediation layer, the inventory of alternative action paths and the pending-action state model

text.en: Check the approval policy in the tool-mediation layer before any call with a side effect goes out.
Inventory other paths to the same effect and remove generic tools that would bypass the gate.
Store the pending action as a minimal encrypted record holding no bearer credentials.
Bind each approval to a digest of the resolved action and give it a validity period.
Re-check conditions that may have changed while the action waited before releasing it.
Use idempotency keys the downstream system enforces, and park ambiguous results as outcome-unknown for a person.

title.en: Configure approver routing and an authenticated decision screen for gated actions

description.en: Route each pending action to approvers holding delegated authority for its class and tier. Notifications may go anywhere, but the decision must be taken in an authenticated, replay-resistant interface that shows the resolved action, its digest and the triggering rule, marks the agent's own rationale as untrusted, and offers reject and escalate as easily as approve. Neither the requester nor the agent may approve; set a deadline with a default on expiry. Attach the routing rules and a screenshot of the decision screen.

evidenceHint.en: Approver routing rules per action class and tier, and the decision screen showing the resolved action, digest, rule and untrusted-rationale label

text.en: Map each action class and tier to the roles authorised to decide it.
Build the decision step in an authenticated interface rather than email replies or chat reactions.
Show the resolved parameters, digest and triggering rule, and label the agent's rationale as untrusted.
Prevent the requester, the agent and shared accounts from recording a decision.
Set a deadline on each pending action and the default outcome or escalation on expiry.
Treat any edit to the action as a new version that is classified and approved again.

title.en: Record each standing pre-approval with its grantor, scope, environment and expiry

description.en: When someone approves a class of actions in advance instead of one at a time, treat it as a risk acceptance. Confirm the grantor holds authority for what the tool can reach, limit the grant to named tools with argument constraints in a stated environment and credential set, give it an expiry, and never allow it for generic tools such as a shell or unrestricted web requests. Link every action released under the grant back to it. Attach the grant register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Register of standing pre-approvals, each with grantor, tools and argument constraints, environment, grant and expiry times, revocation and linked actions

text.en: Confirm the grantor's delegated authority covers everything the granted tool can reach.
Record the named tools and argument constraints the grant covers.
Record the environment and credential set the grant applies to and its expiry.
Refuse grants on shells, unrestricted web requests, database clients or browser drivers.
Link each action released under the grant to its register entry.
Record revocations and expire grants that have gone unused.

title.en: Report gate hit-rate, rejection rate and pending backlog for each gated action class

description.en: Gating too much leads to rubber-stamping, so measure the gate. For each action class, report how often the gate fired, how often approvers rejected, how long items waited and how many expired, and how far standing grants are growing. Treat an approval rate near total, or users repeatedly opting out of prompts, as a sign the threshold is wrong and record the policy change considered. Attach the report.

evidenceHint.en: Gate metrics report per action class showing hit-rate, rejection rate, wait times, expiries, standing-grant growth and policy changes considered

text.en: Extract the number of gated actions per class for the period.
Calculate the approval and rejection rates and the time items waited for a decision.
Count expired and escalated items and the size of the pending backlog.
Measure growth in standing grants for each action class.
Record any threshold or policy change the figures suggest and who decided on it.

title.en: Attempt to run a gated agent action without a valid approval

description.en: Attack the gate as an adversary would: try to run a designated action with no approval, through an unmediated alternative path, by self-approving, by retrying to cause a second execution, by changing parameters after approval, and by submitting a decision after the deadline. Each attempt should fail and be recorded. Attach the test plan and results, with remediation for any success.

evidenceHint.en: Adversarial gate test results listing each attempt, its outcome and remediation for any that succeeded

text.en: Attempt a designated action with no approval through the normal tool path.
Attempt the same effect through an alternative path that skips the gate.
Attempt to approve the action as its requester or through the agent.
Force a retry after release and check the action did not execute twice.
Change the action's parameters after approval and confirm the approval no longer applies.
Submit a decision after the deadline and confirm it is rejected.

templates.title: Agents load only skills and plugins whose reviewed version is verified at load time
templates.description: Every skill or plugin an agent loads comes from a controlled internal source, was approved after review of its instructions, code and dependencies, matches the integrity value registered for that approved version, and is re-reviewed when it changes.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / Application Security Lead
templates.objective: To prevent an agent from loading a skill or plugin whose instructions, bundled code or dependencies were never reviewed, or that changed after approval.
templates.successCriteria:
Installed skills are inventoried with source, version and whether they bundle code or install packages.
Each approved skill has a review record covering instruction text, bundled scripts and dependencies, with pinned dependency versions.
Skills are loaded solely from the internal repository, and environments where integrity checks are enabled refuse a skill whose hash differs from its registered value.
Updated skills are re-reviewed against the approved version before the allowlist changes.
Loads of unapproved skills are logged and investigated.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the skill inventory for each agent environment and the allowlist of approved skill versions.
Obtain the review record for each approved skill, including instruction review, code review, dependency list and lockfile.
Obtain the configuration of the internal skill repository and of workstation or agent skill directories.
Obtain the registered integrity values and the load-time verification configuration, where used.
Obtain skill load and dependency installation logs, and the re-review records for skills updated in the period.

Analysis:
Compare installed skills in a sample of environments with the allowlist and list any not on it.
Confirm each approved skill has a review record dated before approval that addresses instructions, scripts and dependencies, and that its dependencies are pinned.
Attempt to place an unreviewed skill in a managed skill directory and confirm it is refused or alerted on.
Alter one byte of an approved skill in a test environment and confirm load-time verification refuses it.
Check that each skill updated in the period was re-reviewed before its new version was allowlisted, within the turnaround the organisation set.

Output:
A per-environment list of skills installed outside the allowlist.
A per-skill table of review coverage, pinned dependencies and integrity verification.
A list of updates allowlisted without re-review and of unapproved loads not investigated.

title.en: Inventory the skills and plugins loaded into each agent environment

description.en: For every agent environment, including developer workstations running coding agents, list each skill or plugin present, where it was obtained, its version, whether it is instructions only or also ships scripts, and any packages it tells the agent to install. Attach the inventory per environment with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Skill and plugin inventory per agent environment, giving source, version, bundled code and declared package installs

text.en: List the skill and plugin directories each agent tool reads in every environment.
Record each skill's origin, such as a public source or the internal repository.
Record the version or commit of every skill found.
Note whether each skill ships executable scripts in addition to its instruction files.
List every package whose installation each skill asks the agent to perform.

title.en: Restrict agent environments so skills come solely from the approved internal repository

description.en: Keep approved skill versions in an internal repository under version control, point agent tools at it, and take away users' ability to write into the skill folders of managed machines so nobody can add a skill on their own. Where machines cannot be locked down, log every skill load and alert on anything not approved. Attach the repository setup and the directory permission settings.

evidenceHint.en: Internal skill repository configuration, managed directory permissions and, for unmanaged machines, the load logging and alert rule

text.en: Create the internal version-controlled repository that holds approved skill versions.
Point each agent tool's skill path at the managed repository copy.
Revoke user write permission on the skill folders of managed workstations and agent hosts.
Configure logging of skill loads and alerts for unapproved ones where locking is not possible.
Record the machines covered by each approach and file the settings.

title.en: Review each submitted skill's instructions, bundled scripts and dependencies before approval

description.en: Read the skill's instruction files for directions that override policy, reach beyond its stated purpose, touch credentials or agent configuration, or send data out; examine bundled scripts for file access outside the working area, network calls, process launches and persistence; and check every package it installs for legitimacy, known vulnerabilities and its own dependencies, pinning each to a version. Automated scanning may triage but a person decides. Attach the review record and the lockfile.
