evidenceHint.en: Skill review record with instruction, code and dependency findings, the reviewer's decision, and the pinned dependency lockfile

text.en: Compare what the instructions tell the agent to do with the skill's stated purpose.
Flag instructions that read credentials, change agent settings or send data externally.
Inspect every bundled script for file, network, process and persistence behaviour.
Scan bundled files for invisible characters and look-alike letters in code or links.
Check each package for typosquatting and known vulnerabilities, then pin its version.
Record the reviewer, findings and approve or reject decision before allowlisting.

title.en: Register an integrity hash for each approved skill version and refuse loads that do not match

description.en: When a skill version is approved, compute a cryptographic hash or signature over its full bundle and store it with the allowlist entry. Configure agent environments to verify the bundle against that value at load and refuse a mismatch, installing dependencies only from the approved lockfile. Where the agent tool cannot verify natively, record the wrapper or check used instead. Attach the registered values and the verification configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Register of integrity values per approved skill version and the load-time verification configuration

text.en: Compute a hash or signature over the complete bundle of each approved skill version.
Store the value with the allowlist entry for that exact version.
Configure load-time verification to refuse any bundle whose value differs.
Install skill dependencies only from the approved lockfile, not from instruction text.
Test the check by altering a copy of a skill and confirming it is refused.

title.en: Reassess skill updates against the approved version before changing the allowlist

description.en: When a skill's author releases a new version, compare it with the approved one, focusing on changed instructions, new or modified scripts and new dependencies, and repeat the review on what changed before the new version and its integrity value replace the old ones. Track turnaround against the target the organisation set for critical and other skills, and re-assess approved skills when an advisory affects one of their dependencies. Attach the update review log.

evidenceHint.en: Update review log per skill: the difference examined, the decision, the date allowlisted, and dependency advisories acted on

text.en: Record the re-review turnaround targets you set for critical and for other skills.
Produce a difference between the new and approved versions of the skill bundle.
Review changed instructions, scripts and dependencies with the same checks as a new skill.
Replace the allowlist entry and integrity value only after the decision is recorded.
Re-assess skills whose pinned dependencies are named in a new vulnerability advisory.

title.en: Reconcile skill load logs with the allowlist and retire unmaintained skills

description.en: Compare the skill loads and dependency installs logged in the period with the allowlist, investigate every load of an unapproved or unmatched version, and identify approved skills whose authors have stopped maintaining them, that carry unfixed vulnerabilities or whose risk has changed, removing them from the allowlist. Attach the reconciliation and the retirement list.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of logged skill loads against the allowlist, investigation notes and the list of skills retired

text.en: Extract the period's skill load and package installation events from central logs.
Match each event to an allowlisted skill version and list those with no match.
Record the investigation outcome for every unapproved or mismatched load.
List approved skills that are unmaintained or carry unfixed vulnerabilities.
Remove retired skills from the allowlist and repository and note the date.

templates.title: Leakage of sensitive data through AI prompts, outputs, providers and model artefacts is prevented and detected
templates.description: Every path by which session data, training data or model weights can leave the organisation through an AI system is mapped and safeguarded, and planted markers and monitoring raise an incident when something escapes anyway.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: CISO / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To prevent sensitive prompts, responses, training sets and model weights escaping through AI systems and their providers, and to detect and respond to any leak that does occur.
templates.successCriteria:
Every AI egress path for session data, training data and model weights is mapped, impact-rated and owned.
Each external model provider has a dated record of observed transport encryption, endpoint type, retention of logs and sessions, and training use of submitted data.
Canary markers or data fingerprints are active at each AI gateway and ingestion point named in the map, and each is listed in a register.
Every leak alert and canary sighting in the period has a triage outcome, and confirmed leaks carry an incident reference.
A planted test marker was detected and escalated in the most recent detection exercise.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the AI egress map with its impact ratings and the date it was last revised.
Obtain the provider safeguard records, with the evidence behind each entry: connection test output, endpoint configuration, provider documentation or attestation reports.
Obtain the canary and fingerprint register and the configuration that generates and inserts the markers.
Obtain the leak alert log, the guardrail log extracts reviewed for extraction attempts, and the incident records opened from either.
Obtain the report of the latest end-to-end detection exercise.

Analysis:
Compare the egress map with architecture records, procurement records and network egress logs to find AI providers or data flows it does not show.
For each provider, confirm the record is backed by evidence rather than assertion, and note any provider still retaining data or allowed to train on it.
Trace each high-impact path to at least one marker in the register and confirm the scanner covers the sources where that marker would surface.
Sample alerts and confirm each was triaged and that confirmed leaks followed the incident response plan.
Check that the exercise marker was found and that the alert reached the people the plan names.

Output:
A list of egress paths missing from the map or without a marker.
A provider table showing which safeguards are evidenced and which are only claimed.
A statement of whether detection worked in the exercise, with any delay or gap in escalation.

title.en: Map the egress paths for AI session data, training data and model weights

description.en: Trace where prompts, responses and intermediate data travel for each AI system, where proprietary training and fine-tuning sets are copied, and where model weights and configurations are stored or could be exported. Include every externally hosted model provider. Rate each path by the harm a leak would cause so the strongest safeguards go to the worst outcomes. Attach the map with its ratings and date.

evidenceHint.en: AI egress map, one row per path, naming the data type, destination, transport, owner and impact rating

text.en: List each AI system and the prompts, responses and intermediate data it sends anywhere.
Add every external model provider or hosted endpoint those systems call.
Record where training and fine-tuning datasets are copied and who can export them.
Record where model weights and configurations are stored and how they could be copied out.
Rate each path for the impact of a leak and name an owner for it.
Date the map and note the person who compiled it.

title.en: Verify transport, endpoint and data persistence safeguards for each AI provider

description.en: For every external provider on the egress map, test and record the transport encryption actually negotiated, whether traffic uses a private endpoint or dedicated capacity inside your own cloud tenant, how long the provider keeps logs and session data, whether submitted data can train its general models, what caching it applies, and what evidence it gives for isolating tenants (certification reports, penetration test summaries). Negotiating the contract terms themselves belongs to the legal and contractual control; this task checks what is in force. Attach the per-provider record.

evidenceHint.en: Per-provider safeguard record with test output, endpoint configuration, persistence and training-use settings, caching disclosure and isolation evidence

text.en: Capture the protocol version negotiated on a live connection to each provider.
Record whether each provider is reached through a private endpoint or the public internet.
Record the persistence period the provider applies to logs and session data, with its source.
Record whether submitted data may be used for training and where that setting is held.
Note any caching or performance optimisation the provider discloses that keeps copies of data.
File the tenant isolation evidence the provider supplied, with its date.

title.en: Deploy canary markers and data fingerprints at AI gateways and ingestion pipelines

description.en: Generate unique, harmless markers and hashes of sensitive records, and insert them where data enters AI systems: the API gateway in front of model providers and the pipelines that load data for training or retrieval. Register every marker with where and when it was planted, and configure scanning of the external sources where an escaped marker would appear. Attach the register and the scanner configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Canary and fingerprint register, one row per marker with location and date planted, plus the external scanning configuration

text.en: Choose the high-impact paths from the egress map that will carry markers.
Generate unique markers that carry no real customer or business information.
Compute fingerprints of the sensitive records flowing through those paths.
Insert the markers at the gateway or pipeline serving each chosen path.
Configure scanning of public and underground sources for the markers and fingerprints.
Record each marker in the register with its location, path and planting date.

title.en: Triage leak alerts and canary sightings through the incident response plan

description.en: Each time the scanner reports a marker or fingerprint outside the organisation, or another monitor flags a likely AI data leak, the security operations team assesses it and, where it is real, opens an incident under the response plan. Record the alert, the assessment and the outcome. Attach the alert log for the period with incident references.

evidenceHint.en: Leak alert log for the period, giving alert time, source, triage decision and incident reference for confirmed leaks

text.en: Log every scanner hit or leak alert with its time, marker and the source where it surfaced.
Identify which path and provider the surfaced marker was planted on.
Decide whether the alert is a real leak or a false alarm and record the reason.
Open an incident under the response plan for each confirmed leak and note its reference.
Record any containment taken, such as suspending the affected provider path.

title.en: Investigate guardrail logs for prompt patterns aimed at extracting training data

description.en: Read the logs produced by the input and output guardrails for repeated or crafted prompts that try to make a model reproduce its training data, and follow up the suspicious ones. Operating the guardrails themselves belongs to the filtering control; this task looks for extraction attempts in what they record. Attach the review record with the cases followed up.

evidenceHint.en: Guardrail log review record listing the suspicious prompt patterns found, the users or systems involved and the follow-up on each

text.en: Pull the guardrail block and flag events for the period under review.
Group the events by user or calling system to spot repeated probing.
Mark the patterns that look designed to recover training records or memorised text.
Open a follow-up for each suspicious pattern, naming who is investigating it.
Record whether any attempt appears to have retrieved training data.

title.en: Run a detection exercise with a planted test canary

description.en: Deliberately place a test marker where the scanner should find it, without exposing real data, and confirm the alert fires, reaches security operations and is handled under the response plan. Note the time from placement to alert. Record also whether model weight fingerprinting or watermarking has been evaluated for your proprietary models and what was decided. Attach the exercise report.

evidenceHint.en: Detection exercise report giving the marker used, placement and alert times, escalation path followed and gaps found

text.en: Agree the exercise scope and test marker with the owner of the response plan.
Place the test marker in a location the scanner is configured to search.
Record when the alert fired and who received it.
Check that the handling followed the steps in the incident response plan.
Note whether weight fingerprinting or watermarking has been evaluated and the decision.
List each gap found with an owner for its fix.

templates.title: AI system behaviour logged, traced and watched against baselines
templates.description: Every AI system in scope sends structured telemetry about its interactions, model calls, resource use, security events and active versions to a central platform, where dashboards and anomaly alerts compare it with an established baseline.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / Head of IT Operations
templates.objective: To give operators and responders enough visibility into how each AI system behaves to spot anomalies, diagnose faults and reconstruct incidents quickly.
templates.successCriteria:
Each AI system in scope has a recorded telemetry specification naming what it must emit, its owner and the teams that consume it.
Logs and traces from every in-scope system reach the central log platform and name the model, data and component versions active at the time.
Each monitored metric has a recorded baseline, and alert rules fire on the deviations the organisation defined.
Every telemetry store applies the retention period the organisation chose.
Signals, thresholds and dashboards were reassessed in the period and the outcome recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the AI system inventory and, for each system in scope, the telemetry specification listing the events, metrics and traces it must emit.
Obtain the central log platform's list of sources and a sample of log records and traces from each system for the period.
Obtain the baseline records, alert rule definitions and the alert history with dispositions for the period.
Obtain the retention setting of each telemetry store and the most recent observability reassessment record.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory with the platform's sources and list every system sending nothing or only part of its specification.
For a sample of user requests, follow the trace from input through model call, retrieval and tool calls to output, and note any hop without a record.
Check that sampled records carry version identifiers, and that prompt or argument content appears only where the specification allows it.
Confirm each alert rule refers to a recorded baseline and that alerts raised in the period were acknowledged and closed with a reason.
Compare configured retention with the period the organisation set.

Output:
A per-system coverage table showing which telemetry categories arrive and which are missing.
A list of broken traces, unversioned records, alert rules with no baseline and retention mismatches, each with an owner.

title.en: Define the telemetry each AI system must emit and who consumes it

description.en: For every AI system in the inventory, write down the categories of telemetry it must produce: user inputs, model outputs and any confidence data, calls to models, retrieval stores and tools with status and latency, resource consumption, authentication and security-tool events, and the versions in use. Record which content may be captured given privacy and minimisation, and which teams read the data. Attach the specification.

evidenceHint.en: Telemetry specification per AI system, listing event categories, content-capture decisions and consuming teams

text.en: List each AI system in scope with its owner and the components it is built from.
Name the event, metric and trace categories each system must emit, one row per category.
Record whether prompts, outputs and tool arguments are captured in full, summarised or omitted, and why.
Name the teams that read the data, such as operations, security, risk and compliance.
Record the open telemetry naming convention and revision adopted for agent and model operations, if any.
Date the specification and name the person who approved it.

title.en: Route structured logs and distributed traces from each AI system to the central log platform

description.en: Instrument each system with a structured logging library, propagate a trace identifier across services and model, retrieval and tool calls, stamp every record with the active model, data and component versions, and forward everything to the central log or SIEM platform with the retention period the organisation chose. Attach the platform's source list and one end-to-end trace per system.

evidenceHint.en: Central log platform source list plus one complete sample trace per AI system, with the retention setting of each store

text.en: Add structured logging to each component named in the telemetry specification.
Pass a single trace identifier from the user request through every model, retrieval and tool call.
Stamp each record with the model, dataset and component versions active when it was written.
Forward logs and traces to the central platform and confirm each system appears as a source.
Set the retention period the organisation chose on every store holding the telemetry.

title.en: Record baselines and configure anomaly alerts for each monitored AI metric

description.en: Collect telemetry while the system runs normally, over a period the team judges long enough, and record baseline values for latency, throughput, error rates, quality or drift indicators and resource use. Then define the deviations that should alert, route each alert to a responder and publish dashboards for the consuming teams. Attach the baseline record and the exported alert rules.

evidenceHint.en: Baseline record per metric and the exported alert rule set, each rule naming its baseline and responder

text.en: Choose and record the observation window used to establish each baseline.
Record the baseline value or range for every metric the specification lists.
Define the deviation that triggers an alert for each metric and record the reasoning.
Route every alert rule to a named responder queue or rota.
Publish a dashboard per system showing health, quality and security signals against baseline.

title.en: Triage AI system anomaly alerts and log the outcome of each

description.en: Acknowledge each alert, pull the related traces, classify the cause as performance, drift, security, misuse or false alarm, and hand anything that meets the incident criteria to incident handling. Close each alert with its classification and outcome so the history can be audited. Attach the alert log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Alert log for the period with acknowledgement time, classification, linked incident if any and outcome per alert

text.en: Acknowledge each alert and note who picked it up.
Retrieve the traces and logs around the alert and attach them to the record.
Classify the cause as performance, drift, security, misuse or false alarm.
Open an incident for any alert that meets the organisation's incident criteria.
Close the alert with its outcome and any follow-up action and owner.

title.en: Reassess collected AI telemetry signals, alert thresholds and dashboards against current risks

description.en: On the cadence the organisation set, compare the specification with what actually arrives, trace a sample of requests end to end, look at rules that never fired or fired too often, and check whether new risks, components or a newer revision of the adopted naming convention call for changes. Attach the record with each change agreed and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Observability reassessment record listing coverage gaps, threshold changes, convention revision decisions and owners

text.en: Compare each system's specification with the categories arriving on the central platform.
Trace a sample of requests end to end and record any hop that left no record.
List alert rules that never fired or fired mostly as false alarms, and decide on each.
Check whether new components, risks or obligations need extra signals or dashboards.
Record whether to move to a newer revision of the adopted telemetry convention.
Enter each agreed change with its owner and target date.

templates.title: AI spend capped, attributed to its owner and alerted on before budgets run out
templates.description: Usage-priced AI services sit under an organisation-wide cap and cascading budgets, every cost is attributed to an owner, staged and anomaly alerts fire before limits are hit, and hard limits throttle or suspend consumption automatically.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: FinOps Lead / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To ensure accidental or deliberate overconsumption of AI services is detected and stopped before it causes unplanned cost or a service cut-off.
templates.successCriteria:
Every usage-priced AI service is recorded with its billing account and the cost owner accountable for it.
An organisation-wide cap and budgets at department, project and key level are set, with the values recorded.
Alerts fire at the staged thresholds the organisation chose and on spending anomalies, each with an escalation route.
Reaching a hard limit throttles or suspends non-critical consumption automatically.
Each alert is investigated and classed as legitimate use, misconfiguration or attack.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of usage-priced AI services with billing account, cost centre and cost owner.
Obtain the cap, budget and per-key token or request quota settings at each level, from the provider billing console, infrastructure-as-code or gateway.
Obtain the alert configuration with thresholds and escalation recipients.
Obtain the automatic throttling or suspension rule for hard limits.
Obtain the spend alert log with investigation outcomes, and the budget-versus-actual report for the period.

Analysis:
Compare billing data with the register and name any AI spend with no recorded owner.
Confirm a cap or budget exists at each level the organisation defined and that lower budgets sum within higher ones.
Confirm alerts are set at the chosen thresholds and that a sampled alert reached its recipients.
Confirm the hard-limit rule is active and, where safe, trigger it in a test account.
Sample alerts and confirm each has a recorded classification and action.
Review variances between budget and actual and confirm each significant one has a cause.

Output:
A list of unattributed AI spend and levels without a budget.
A list of alerts without an investigation outcome.
A variance summary naming the causes found.

title.en: Register every usage-priced AI service with its billing account and cost owner

description.en: List each AI service the organisation pays for by consumption, such as hosted model APIs and compute-heavy AI workloads, with the billing account it charges to, the cost centre, the projects and use cases drawing on it, and the person accountable for its cost. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of usage-priced AI services naming billing account, cost centre, consuming projects and cost owner

text.en: Pull every AI-related line from provider invoices and cloud billing exports.
Match each service to its billing account and cost centre.
List the projects, applications and use cases consuming each service.
Name the person accountable for the cost of each service.

title.en: Set the organisation-wide AI spending cap and the budgets cascading beneath it

description.en: Fix a hard spending cap for AI services at organisation level through the payment provider or cloud billing controls, then allocate budgets to departments, projects and environments and token or request quotas to individual keys and users, expressed where possible as infrastructure-as-code. Record the values you chose and confirm lower budgets fit within higher ones. Attach the settings.

evidenceHint.en: Cap and budget settings at each level, from billing console or infrastructure-as-code, with the chosen values recorded

text.en: Set the organisation-wide cap in the billing or payment provider controls.
Allocate department and billing-account budgets and record each value.
Declare project and environment quotas in infrastructure-as-code.
Set token and request consumption quotas on each gateway key.
Check that the budgets at each level sum within the level above.

title.en: Configure staged spend alerts and spending-anomaly alerts with escalation recipients

description.en: In the model hosting or cloud platform, set alerts at the percentages of each budget the organisation chooses, with the recipients becoming more senior at each stage, and add detection for unusual spending patterns such as sudden spikes by a key or project. Attach the alert configuration and a test alert received.

evidenceHint.en: Alert configuration listing each threshold, anomaly rule and recipient group, plus a received test alert

text.en: Record the budget percentages you chose as alert thresholds.
Configure an alert at each threshold for every budget in the register.
Assign a recipient group per stage, escalating as spend approaches the limit.
Enable anomaly detection on spend per key, project and service.
Send a test alert and keep the copy that reached its recipients.

title.en: Configure automatic throttling or suspension when an AI hard spend limit is hit

description.en: Define for each hard limit what happens when it is reached: which non-critical services are throttled or suspended, which critical services are kept running, and who is told. Configure the action in the billing controls or gateway and test it in a non-production account. Attach the rule and the test result.

evidenceHint.en: Hard-limit action rule naming the services throttled, suspended or exempted, with the result of a non-production trigger test

text.en: List the services to be throttled or suspended when each hard limit is hit.
List the critical services that stay running and the reason for each.
Configure the cut-off in the billing controls or the API gateway.
Trigger the limit in a non-production account and record what happened.

title.en: Investigate each AI spend alert and classify its cause

description.en: For every threshold, anomaly or suspension alert, find the key, user or project driving the consumption and decide whether it is legitimate use, a misconfiguration or an attempt to run up costs. Apply extra limits where needed, hand suspected attacks to the security incident process, tell affected users, and log the outcome. Attach the alert log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Spend alert log for the period with the consumer identified, cause classification and action taken for each alert

text.en: Identify the key, user or project behind each alert from usage records.
Classify the cause as legitimate use, misconfiguration or attack.
Apply additional quotas or revoke keys where consumption must stop.
Raise a security incident for every alert classed as an attack.
Notify affected users and record the closing action against the alert.

title.en: Compare actual AI spend with budget and charge it back to cost owners

description.en: At each budget period end, compare actual AI consumption with planned spend for every budget, find the cause of each significant variance, charge costs back to the business units that incurred them, and feed the findings into the next budget forecast and into negotiations with providers. Attach the variance report.

evidenceHint.en: Budget-versus-actual report per budget with variance causes, chargeback amounts and forecast adjustments

text.en: Export actual AI spend per budget for the period from billing data.
Compare each figure with its budget and mark the significant variances.
Record the cause of each significant variance after asking its cost owner.
Post chargeback entries to the cost centres that incurred the spend.
Note forecast changes and points to raise with providers.

templates.title: User and expert feedback on AI outputs captured, triaged and acted upon
templates.description: Each AI system offers low-effort channels for users and subject-matter experts to rate and report on its outputs, and every item received is triaged, tracked to a recorded action and, where feasible, answered.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Product Owner / Head of AI Governance
templates.objective: To ensure what users and experts notice about an AI system's outputs reaches the people able to fix it and ends in a recorded change, escalation or reasoned decision.
templates.successCriteria:
Each AI system in scope has a written feedback design naming its purpose, the indicators it measures and who triages it.
Users can rate an output and report a concern from inside the system, and an expert review group has its own route.
Every feedback item received in the period has a severity, an owner and a recorded outcome.
Reports of security flaws, data leakage or harm were passed to incident handling.
Submission rates were tracked, and any decline the organisation treats as significant led to corrective action.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the feedback design for each AI system in scope, naming its purpose, the indicators it supports, its audiences and its triage owner.
Obtain screenshots or configuration of the in-product feedback controls and the route for expert reviewers.
Obtain the feedback register for the period with severity, owner, action and outcome per item, and the trend reports given to governance.

Analysis:
Check that each feedback question maps to a stated performance indicator and that the controls let a user both rate an output and report a concern.
Sample feedback items and confirm each has a severity, an owner, an action or a reasoned decision to take none, and a closure date.
Trace items mentioning injection, leakage, bias or harm to an incident or escalation record.
Compare submission rates across the period and confirm any significant decline was investigated.
For a sample of closed items, confirm the change was deployed and, where feasible, the reporter was told.

Output:
A per-system statement of which feedback channels exist and which indicators they serve.
A list of items left untriaged, closed without action or reason, or not escalated when they should have been, and any unaddressed fall in participation.

title.en: Record the purpose, indicators and triage owner of each AI system's feedback channel

description.en: For each AI system, write down what feedback will be used for, such as prompt refinement, knowledge base corrections, drift detection or model refinement, which performance indicators the questions measure, whether it is gathered from all users, a small expert group or both, and who triages it with what severity categories. Attach the design document.

evidenceHint.en: Feedback design per AI system naming purpose, indicators, audiences, severity categories and triage owner

text.en: State the uses the feedback will be put to for this system.
Map each feedback question or rating to a named performance indicator.
Decide whether to collect from all users, a small expert group, or both, and record why.
Define the severity categories used to prioritise incoming items.
Name the person or team who triages feedback and the one who acts on it.

title.en: Add in-product rating and concern-reporting controls to each AI system

description.en: Put a low-effort rating control and a free-text comment beside each output, with a category for harmful, biased, insecure or leaked content, and capture the request, output and version the feedback refers to where privacy allows. Give expert reviewers a separate route, collect any implicit signals the design chose, and tell users how their input is used. Attach screenshots and configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots and configuration of the rating, comment and concern-reporting controls, the expert route and the user notice

text.en: Add a one-click rating control next to each output the system produces.
Add an optional comment field and a category for harmful, biased or insecure content.
Attach the request, output and system version to each submission where privacy permits.
Configure any implicit signals the design chose, such as a quick rephrase or an ignored suggestion.
Set up a separate submission route for the expert review group.
Show users a short notice explaining how their feedback will be used.

title.en: Triage incoming AI feedback and log the action taken on each item

description.en: Classify every item against the severity categories, route reports of injection, data leakage or harm to incident handling, and assign the rest an action such as a prompt change, a knowledge base correction, a documentation update or an escalation to the model team. Record the outcome and, where feasible, tell the reporter. Attach the feedback register.

evidenceHint.en: Feedback register for the period with severity, owner, action, outcome and reporter notification per item

text.en: Assign each new item a severity and an owner from the triage rota.
Pass reports of injection, data leakage or harm to incident handling and link the incident.
Choose an action for each remaining item or record why none is needed.
Record the outcome and the date each item was closed.
Notify the reporter of the outcome where the channel allows it.

title.en: Report feedback trends and participation rates to the AI governance body

description.en: Aggregate ratings over time against the indicators they map to, group free-text comments into themes, and flag declining scores that may point to drift. Track how many people submit feedback and how useful it is; where participation falls, record the corrective step taken, such as simplifying the control or rotating expert reviewers. Attach the report.

evidenceHint.en: Periodic feedback trend report with rating trends, comment themes, submission rates and corrective actions

text.en: Chart each rating against its performance indicator across the reporting period.
Group free-text comments into themes and count the items in each.
Flag sustained falls in ratings that may signal model or data drift.
Report submission rates and note any decline the organisation treats as significant.
Record the corrective step taken for any fall in participation.

title.en: Sample closed feedback items to confirm each fix took effect

description.en: Draw a sample of items closed in the period, confirm the change they led to is live, try to reproduce the original issue, and check that none was closed without either an action or a recorded reason. Attach the sample results with each failure and its follow-up owner.

evidenceHint.en: Sample of closed feedback items with verification result, reproduction attempt and follow-up owner for each failure

text.en: Select a sample of feedback items closed during the period.
Confirm the change each item led to is deployed in the live system.
Attempt to reproduce the originally reported behaviour and record the result.
Flag items closed with neither an action nor a recorded reason.
Assign an owner to every item that failed verification.

templates.title: AI-generated answers traceable to the specific sources behind them
templates.description: Informational answers from in-scope AI systems carry citations to the exact passage and version of the source used, uncited content is labelled as such, and citation accuracy and link health are checked.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Engineering Lead / Knowledge Management Owner
templates.objective: To let users, reviewers and auditors check any informational claim an AI system makes against the exact source and version it relied on, exposing unsupported content.
templates.successCriteria:
Each in-scope retrieval pipeline keeps a recorded link between every retrieved chunk and the part of the answer built from it.
Indexed content carries a stable identifier, title, position within the document and a version or updated date.
Sampled citations point to passages that support the claim they are attached to.
Answers not grounded in retrieved material are labelled as such and carry no citation.
Cited links and source versions were checked in the period and broken or changed ones handled.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of AI systems that present informational answers and the sources each one draws on.
Obtain the retrieval pipeline configuration showing how chunks are identified and which source metadata travels with them.
Obtain the user guidance and technical documentation describing the citation mechanism and its limits.
Obtain the link and version check results for the period and the latest citation accuracy sample.

Analysis:
Confirm every inventoried system has a pipeline that carries chunk identifiers into the answer.
Sample indexed chunks and check each holds an identifier, title, location in the document and version or date.
Sample answers, open every cited passage and judge whether it supports the specific claim, noting citations that are too broad.
Look in the sample for claims with no citation and no uncited label, and for references that do not exist.
Compare the link check results with the cited sources and confirm broken or changed links were handled.

Output:
A per-system statement of citation coverage and metadata completeness.
A list of unsupported, over-broad or fabricated citations, unlabelled uncited claims and unhandled broken links, each with an owner.

title.en: Inventory the AI systems that present informational answers and the sources each draws on

description.en: List every AI system whose output is meant to inform a decision or answer a question, the knowledge bases, document stores and external sites each retrieves from, and whether each source is an authoritative internal repository or a less curated one. Attach the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of informational AI systems, one row per system and source, with source type and persistence of its identifiers

text.en: List each AI system that generates informational answers, with its owner.
Record every knowledge base, document store or external site each system retrieves from.
Mark each source as an authoritative internal repository or a less curated one.
Note whether each source gives its content stable, persistent identifiers.

title.en: Configure retrieval pipelines to carry chunk identifiers and source metadata into each answer

description.en: Split source documents into uniquely addressable chunks, keep their title, author, location, page or section and version or updated date through ingestion, and have the pipeline record which chunk supports which part of the answer. Content not grounded in a retrieved chunk is labelled as uncited and never given a made-up reference. Attach the configuration and a sample answer with its citations.

evidenceHint.en: Pipeline configuration showing chunking, preserved metadata and chunk-to-answer linkage, plus one cited sample answer

text.en: Choose a chunking method that gives every chunk a unique, addressable identifier.
Preserve title, author, location, page or section and version date for every chunk at ingestion.
Record which retrieved chunk supports each sentence or segment of the generated answer.
Label any answer content not drawn from a retrieved chunk as uncited.
Block the system from emitting a reference that does not match a retrieved chunk.
Display citations in the interface with a way to open the source or read a snippet from it.

title.en: Publish user guidance and technical documentation on how AI citations are produced and their limits

description.en: Write a short guide for users explaining what the citation markers mean, how to open the source, and that a citation shows where a statement came from rather than proving the source is correct or current. Write a technical note for engineers and auditors describing the citation mechanism, the source types referenced and known weaknesses. Attach both.

evidenceHint.en: User guide on reading AI citations and the technical citation-mechanism note, each with its publication date

text.en: Explain in the user guide what each citation marker means and how to open the source.
State that a citation identifies origin and does not vouch for the source's accuracy or currency.
Describe the citation mechanism and its logic in the technical note.
List the types of source referenced and how each is identified.
Record the known limitations and inaccuracies of the citation process.

title.en: Check cited links and source versions for breakage or change

description.en: On the cadence the organisation chose, run a link check over every URL and document reference the systems cite, detect sources whose content has changed or been archived since it was indexed, and record how each was handled: re-indexed, cached, replaced by a persistent identifier or marked as updated. Attach the check results.

evidenceHint.en: Link and version check report listing each broken or changed cited source and how it was handled

text.en: Run an automated check over every cited URL and internal document reference.
Detect sources whose content or version changed after they were indexed.
Record a handling decision for each broken or changed source.
Prefer persistent identifiers such as DOIs or document IDs when replacing a broken link.

title.en: Test a sample of AI answers for citation accuracy and relevance

description.en: Draw a sample of answers from each in-scope system, open every cited passage and judge whether it supports the exact claim it is attached to, note citations that point to a whole document when a passage was needed, and look for uncited claims missing their label or references to sources that do not exist. Attach the sample results with each failure and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Citation accuracy sample per system with a verdict per citation and an owner for each failure

text.en: Select a sample of recent answers from each in-scope system.
Open each cited passage and record whether it supports the specific claim.
Note citations that are too broad to verify the claim they accompany.
Record any claim that lacks both a citation and an uncited label.
Record any reference to a source or passage that does not exist.
Assign each failure an owner and a fix.

templates.title: Model-based output grading calibrated against human experts and overseen by people
templates.description: A judge model grades sampled outputs of the AI system against a written rubric, its verdicts are benchmarked against subject-matter expert grading, and people review what it flags, what it is unsure of and a sample of what it passes.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Evaluation Lead / Model Risk Owner
templates.objective: To grade AI outputs at a scale people cannot reach by hand while holding evidence that the automated judge agrees with expert human judgement.
templates.successCriteria:
A rubric for each judged system defines what is assessed, the inputs the judge receives and its output format, including a rationale.
The judge's agreement with expert labels on a representative set is recorded with the metrics the organisation chose, against the level it set.
The judge grades a production sample at the cadence and sample size the organisation recorded.
Flagged outputs, low-confidence verdicts and a random sample of passes are reviewed by a person and escalated where confirmed.
Calibration was repeated in the period and after every rubric or judge change.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the rubric for each judged system, naming the qualities assessed, the inputs passed to the judge, the output format and the judge model and version.
Obtain the calibration set, the expert labels, the judge's verdicts on the same items and the agreement metrics computed.
Obtain the sampling specification and the judge's production verdicts for the period.
Obtain the human review queue history and escalation records for the period.

Analysis:
Confirm the calibration was completed before the judge's scores were used, and recompute the agreement metrics from the raw labels and verdicts.
Read the confusion matrix or score correlation for systematic disagreement, such as the judge passing items experts failed.
Compare the agreement achieved with the level the organisation set as acceptable.
Check the production sample matches the recorded cadence and size and that each verdict carries a rationale.
Confirm flagged, low-confidence and randomly sampled passed verdicts reached a reviewer and that confirmed issues were escalated.
Check a recalibration followed every change of rubric, judge model or primary system.

Output:
A per-system statement of judge agreement against the accepted level, with the direction of any systematic error.
A list of unreviewed flags, missed samples and changes made without recalibration, each with an owner.

title.en: Write the judge rubric, inputs and output format for each evaluated AI system

description.en: For each system whose outputs will be graded by a model, set down which qualities the judge assesses, such as factual consistency with a supplied source, relevance, safety or presence of personal data, the inputs it receives with each item, and the exact verdict format, including a short rationale. Name the judge model and version. Attach the rubric.

evidenceHint.en: Judge rubric per system naming assessed qualities, inputs, verdict format and the judge model and version

text.en: List the qualities of the primary system's output the judge will assess.
Define each quality with pass and fail examples a reviewer would agree with.
Specify the inputs passed to the judge: the original request, the output, any source context and the rubric.
Fix the verdict format as a score or label together with a short written rationale.
Record the judge model, its version and the prompt used to instruct it.

title.en: Measure the judge model against expert human grading on a labelled set

description.en: Assemble outputs from the primary system that reflect real use, have subject-matter experts label each one against the rubric without seeing the judge's verdict, run the judge over the same set, and compute agreement using the metrics that fit the verdict type. Refine the prompt or the judge until agreement reaches the level the organisation set. Attach the set, labels, verdicts and metrics.

evidenceHint.en: Calibration pack with the labelled set, judge verdicts, agreement metrics, confusion matrix and the accepted level

text.en: Draw a set of primary-system outputs that reflects the cases seen in real use.
Have experts label every item against the rubric without sight of the judge's verdict.
Run the judge over the same items and store its verdicts and rationales.
Compute precision, recall and F1 for label verdicts or rank correlation for numeric scores.
Inspect the confusion matrix for one-sided disagreement and record what it shows.
Record the agreement level the organisation accepts and whether the judge reached it.

title.en: Run the judge over sampled production outputs at the recorded cadence

description.en: Record how production outputs are sampled, how many, and whether grading runs in batches or close to real time, scaled to how critical the system is. Run the judge on that schedule, store each verdict with its rationale and the versions involved, and trend the scores so a fall in quality is visible. Attach the sampling specification and the verdict log.

evidenceHint.en: Sampling specification and production verdict log with rationale, versions and score trend for the period

text.en: Record the sampling method, sample size and run cadence chosen for each system.
Run the judge on each scheduled sample and confirm no run was skipped.
Store every verdict with its rationale and the primary and judge model versions.
Chart score trends across runs and flag sustained declines.
Pass recurring weaknesses the judge finds to the team that owns the primary system.

title.en: Route judge-flagged and low-confidence verdicts to human reviewers and escalate confirmed issues

description.en: Send every output the judge fails, every verdict it marks as uncertain, and a random sample of outputs it passes to a human reviewer. The reviewer confirms or overturns the verdict, and a confirmed serious issue is escalated to the relevant team, such as security, legal or compliance. Attach the review queue history and escalation records.

evidenceHint.en: Human review queue history with reviewer decision per item and the escalation record for each confirmed issue

text.en: Queue every failed verdict for review by a named person.
Queue every verdict the judge marks as low confidence.
Queue a random sample of passed verdicts to look for missed failures.
Record the reviewer's confirmation or reversal of each queued verdict.
Escalate each confirmed serious issue to the responsible team and link the record.

title.en: Re-evaluate the judge's calibration after rubric, judge model or primary system changes

description.en: Whenever the rubric, the judge model or the primary system changes, and on the cadence the organisation set otherwise, draw a fresh labelled sample, re-measure agreement with experts, compare it with the last calibration, and decide whether to keep, refine or replace the judge. Use the reversal rate from human review as an extra signal. Attach the recalibration record.

evidenceHint.en: Recalibration record comparing current and previous agreement, the reversal rate and the keep, refine or replace decision

text.en: List the rubric, judge model and primary system changes made since the last calibration.
Draw a fresh sample and have experts label it against the current rubric.
Re-measure agreement and compare it with the previous calibration result.
Include the rate at which human reviewers overturned the judge's verdicts.
Record the decision to keep, refine or replace the judge, with its owner.

templates.title: Retrieval results honour the access permissions of the source documents they came from
templates.description: Content ingested into AI retrieval carries its source permissions, every query is filtered by the asking user's entitlements before the model sees anything, and bypasses are hunted for.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / CISO
templates.objective: To stop an AI system becoming a route to information a user could not open at its source, by carrying source permissions into retrieval and checking they hold.
templates.successCriteria:
Every repository feeding a retrieval index has its permission model documented and mapped to identity provider groups.
Each index has a recorded enforcement pattern, none relying only on instructions to the model.
Retrieved chunks are filtered by the querying user's entitlements before being passed to the model.
Permission changes at a source reach the index within the delay the organisation has accepted.
Red-team tests and entitlement reconciliation found no unresolved path to restricted content.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the catalogue of source repositories with their permission models and the mapping to identity provider groups.
Obtain the enforcement design record for each retrieval index, including any consolidation of permissions into broader tiers and its risk assessment.
Obtain the ingestion configuration that tags chunks with permissions and the query-time filter configuration.
Obtain retrieval logs showing queries, retrieved source identifiers and responses, and the monitoring review records.
Obtain the latest red-team report and the entitlement reconciliation.

Analysis:
Pick sample documents with restricted permissions at source and confirm their chunks carry matching tags in the index.
Query as test users with and without entitlement and confirm restricted chunks are withheld from the model's context, not just hidden in the answer.
Change a permission at a source and measure how long the index takes to reflect it.
Check that no index depends on system prompt instructions as its only control.
Compare the population of AI system users against source permissions to find users who could reach content they cannot open at source.

Output:
A per-index statement of the pattern used and whether testing confirmed it.
The measured propagation delay against the accepted delay.
A list of bypass paths and over-entitled users, with fixes and owners.

title.en: Catalogue the permission model of every repository feeding a retrieval index

description.en: For each wiki, file share, database or document management system that supplies an AI retrieval index, document how access is granted there: access control lists, roles, groups and any finer-grained restriction, such as at paragraph or cell level. Map those permissions to users and groups in the organisation's identity provider. Attach the catalogue and mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Source permission catalogue, one row per repository, with its permission model, granularity and mapping to identity provider groups

text.en: List every repository that feeds documents or records into a retrieval index.
Describe how each grants access: lists, roles, groups or attributes.
Note the finest granularity at which each restricts access.
Map each source permission to identity provider users or groups.
Flag permissions that have no clean equivalent in the identity provider.

title.en: Choose and record the permission enforcement pattern for each retrieval index

description.en: Decide for each index whether permissions will be enforced natively in the vector or graph store at document or chunk level, by splitting content into separate indexes per access domain, by an application layer that constrains queries and filters responses, or by permission metadata filtered at query time. If granular permissions are merged into broader tiers, record the risk assessment. Record that system prompt instructions are not an acceptable enforcement mechanism. Attach the design record.

evidenceHint.en: Enforcement design record per index naming the pattern chosen, the reasons, any permission consolidation and its risk assessment

text.en: Assess whether each target store supports access control at document or chunk level.
Choose the pattern for each index and record why it fits that store.
Record any merging of source permissions into broader tiers with its risk assessment.
State explicitly that model instructions alone are not used to restrict content.
Date the design record and name who made each pattern choice.

title.en: Label ingested chunks with source permissions and filter retrieval by user entitlement

description.en: Extend ingestion so each chunk or index entry carries the permissions, sensitivity and authorised groups of the document it came from, and configure retrieval to resolve the querying user's entitlements from the identity provider and drop non-matching chunks before anything reaches the model. Propagate permission changes at the source to the index. Attach the configuration and a test showing a restricted chunk withheld.

evidenceHint.en: Ingestion tagging and query-time filter configuration, plus a test record showing a restricted chunk withheld from an unentitled user

text.en: Add source permission and sensitivity metadata to every chunk at ingestion.
Resolve the querying user's groups from the identity provider at query time.
Filter retrieved chunks against those groups before building the model context.
Configure re-ingestion or update of tags when a source permission changes.
Record the propagation delay the organisation accepts for permission changes.
Run a query as an unentitled test user and keep the evidence of the withheld chunk.

title.en: Monitor retrieval logs for answers drawing on content outside the user's entitlements

description.en: Log each query, the user, the source documents behind the chunks retrieved and the response produced, so lineage from answer to source can be followed. Review the logs for retrievals that do not match the user's known entitlements, queries probing beyond a user's usual scope and other unusual patterns, and follow up each finding. Attach the review record.

evidenceHint.en: Retrieval log review record listing mismatches between user entitlements and sources used, probing patterns found and follow-up

text.en: Confirm logs record the user, query, source identifiers of retrieved chunks and response.
Compare the sources used for each sampled answer with the user's entitlements.
Look for users repeatedly querying topics outside their normal scope.
Record each mismatch or probing pattern with its investigation owner.
Note whether any restricted content actually reached a user.

title.en: Test the retrieval layer adversarially for bypasses of preserved source permissions

description.en: Using test accounts with known entitlements, try to obtain restricted content through the AI system: adversarial prompts, questions that make the model combine allowed and restricted chunks, recently revoked permissions, and direct calls to the index. Record every attempt and outcome. Attach the test report.

evidenceHint.en: Red-team report listing each bypass attempt, the account used, the result and the fix for each success

text.en: Set up test accounts with known, differing entitlements across sources.
Attempt to retrieve restricted content through crafted and adversarial prompts.
Test questions designed to make the model synthesise restricted and permitted material.
Revoke a permission at source and test whether the index still serves the content.
Try calling the index or vector store directly with each test account.
Record each attempt with its outcome and the fix for each success.

title.en: Reconcile AI system users against the source permissions of ingested content

description.en: Compare the users and groups who can reach each AI retrieval interface with the permissions on the content ingested behind it, and identify anyone who could obtain through the AI system something they cannot open at source, including through aggregation across sources. Attach the reconciliation with each over-entitlement and its fix.

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement reconciliation per retrieval interface listing over-entitled users or groups, the content exposed and the fix

text.en: Export the users and groups with access to each retrieval interface.
Export the source permissions on the content behind that interface.
Identify users who can reach the interface but not some of its content at source.
Check those users are filtered from that content at query time.
Record each over-entitlement with its fix and owner.

templates.title: Agent decisions can be reconstructed at the depth each use case's risk requires
templates.description: Each agent use case has a recorded decision on how much of its decision-making is captured, and the records kept at that depth are enough to reconstruct what the agent did and, where required, why.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / Head of Internal Audit
templates.objective: To keep a record of agent decisions deep enough for each use case's risk that an investigator or reviewer can later reconstruct what the agent did and why.
templates.successCriteria:
Every agent use case has a recorded audit tier with the risk analysis and cost-benefit reasoning behind it.
Use cases above the minimum tier log inputs, data sources, tool invocations, timestamps and final outcomes.
Use cases needing explanation log the agent's reasoning before each tool call, and provider limits on reasoning capture are recorded.
Use cases at the highest tier keep tamper-evident records with full context and are monitored as they run.
A sample of decisions was reconstructed from the records alone, and gaps have owners.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the architecture decision records assigning an audit tier to each agent use case, with their risk and cost-benefit analysis.
Obtain the logging configuration for each use case, showing what is captured for inputs, sources, tool calls, reasoning, context and outcomes.
Obtain the integrity mechanism protecting decision records for the highest tier, and its verification output.
Obtain the latest decision reconstruction exercise and its findings.

Analysis:
Compare the agent use cases in production with the decision records and note any use case without a tier.
Check that each use case's logging captures what its tier calls for and nothing is missing.
Confirm that where a model provider hides reasoning, the limitation is stated in the decision record.
For a sample of decisions, attempt to reconstruct the sequence of inputs, tool calls and outcome from the records alone.
For sampled decisions at the explanation tiers, confirm reasoning was logged before each tool call.
Verify the integrity check on highest-tier records reports no breaks.

Output:
A table of use cases showing assigned tier and whether captured logging matches it.
A list of decisions that could not be reconstructed or explained, integrity breaks found, and owners for each gap.

title.en: Record an architecture decision assigning an audit tier to each agent use case

description.en: For every agent use case, weigh the stakes of its decisions, the regulatory need to explain them, the presence of human oversight, the risk that keeping data creates leakage, and the cost of capturing reasoning, then choose a tier from minimal security logging up to a full tamper-evident trail. Write the analysis and choice as an architecture decision record, noting any model whose internal reasoning cannot be captured. Attach the records.

evidenceHint.en: Architecture decision record per agent use case giving the risk analysis, cost-benefit reasoning, chosen tier and any provider limitation

text.en: List every agent use case in production or approved for production.
Assess each for decision stakes, need for explanation, human oversight and data leakage risk.
Estimate the token and storage cost of capturing reasoning at each candidate tier.
Choose a tier for each use case and record the reasoning in an architecture decision record.
Note any model whose hidden reasoning prevents the full capture the tier would need.

title.en: Configure decision logging to capture inputs, sources, tool calls and outcomes

description.en: For use cases above the minimal tier, log enough to replay what happened in a test environment: the prompts and data inputs, the sources they came from, each tool invocation with its parameters and result, timestamps and the final decision. For minimal-tier use cases, keep the infrastructure security logging the decision record names. Attach the logging configuration and a sample trace.

evidenceHint.en: Logging configuration per use case and a sample decision trace showing inputs, sources, tool calls, timestamps and outcome

text.en: Log the prompt and data inputs each agent decision starts from, with their sources.
Log every tool invocation with its parameters, result and timestamp.
Log the final decision or outcome against a correlation identifier for the run.
Keep authentication and authorisation-failure logging for minimal-tier use cases.
Replay one logged run in a test environment to confirm the trace is sufficient.

title.en: Configure agents in explanation-tier use cases to write their reasoning before each tool call

description.en: Where a use case requires explanation, have the agent produce a plain-language account of its reasoning before it calls a tool, and log that alongside the call, with confidence and alternatives considered where feasible. For the highest tier, add the surrounding customer, business, risk and timing context to each record. Attach the configuration and a sample record with reasoning.

evidenceHint.en: Agent configuration for reasoning capture and a sample decision record showing reasoning logged before each tool call, with context for the highest tier

text.en: Instruct the agent to state its reasoning before each tool call in explanation-tier use cases.
Log the reasoning with the tool call it precedes under the same correlation identifier.
Capture confidence and alternatives considered where the model can provide them.
Add customer, business, risk and timing context to records at the highest tier.
Record where the provider withholds internal reasoning so the gap is visible.

title.en: Configure tamper-evident storage and live monitoring for highest-tier decision records

description.en: Store decision records for the highest-tier use cases so any alteration is detectable, for example append-only storage with hash chaining, restrict who can read them given their privacy and confidentiality sensitivity, verify their integrity on a schedule you set, and monitor them as they are written for anomalous agent decisions. Attach the storage configuration, an integrity verification result and the monitoring rules.

evidenceHint.en: Tamper-evident storage configuration, an integrity verification result and the anomaly monitoring rules for highest-tier decision records

text.en: Write highest-tier decision records to append-only storage with hash chaining or equivalent.
Restrict read access to the records to the roles that investigate or review decisions.
Run the integrity verification at the interval you set and keep each result.
Configure monitoring rules that flag anomalous agent decisions as records arrive.
Record each monitoring alert and how it was resolved.

title.en: Reconstruct a sample of agent decisions from their records alone

description.en: Pick decisions from each tier and, using only the stored records, rebuild what the agent received, which tools it called and what it decided, and for the explanation tiers why. Compare the result with what the use case's tier promised and record every decision that could not be reconstructed or explained. Attach the reconstruction results with gaps and owners.

evidenceHint.en: Decision reconstruction results per sampled decision, with gaps against the assigned tier and an owner for each

text.en: Select a sample of decisions from each audit tier in use.
Rebuild each decision's inputs, tool calls and outcome using only the stored records.
For explanation-tier samples, check that reasoning precedes each tool call.
For highest-tier samples, confirm the integrity check passes for the records used.
Record each decision that could not be reconstructed, with the cause and an owner.

pack.name: FINOS AIGF Baseline Pack
pack.description: One control per FINOS AIGF mitigation, preventative and detective. MI-24 and MI-25 are FINOS drafts and say so in their summary; mark any mitigation that does not fit your AI systems not applicable rather than leaving it open.
